result.output:
has a button for it.

### Logs

Test runs and scored runs keep their output. Read it from a cursor: each page holds up to 128 chunks and the cursor
to continue from.

```sh
cursor=0
while :; do
  page=$(curl -s "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/logs?after=$cursor" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN")
  printf '%s' "$page" | jq -j '.chunks[].text'
  next=$(printf '%s' "$page" | jq .cursor)
  [ "$next" = "$cursor" ] && break
  cursor=$next
done
```

While the run is live, keep polling with a pause until `feed` reports `phase` `done` and its `log_cursor` is no
newer than yours. Or follow them as they arrive, as server-sent events:

```sh
curl -N "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/logs/stream?after=$cursor" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"
```

Each event is one chunk: `id` is its cursor and `data` is `{"at", "stream", "text"}`. Reconnect with
`Last-Event-ID` (an `EventSource` does this by itself) or `?after=` to resume. A comment line (`: heartbeat`) comes
every 15 seconds; once the run has finished and everything is sent, an `end` event closes the stream, and connecting
again answers `204`. All of it at once, as JSON lines:

```sh
curl -o logs.jsonl "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/logs.jsonl" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"
```

To look at one stretch of a run, query its lines by time and content. Times are on the run's clock, as the run page
shows them: `mm:ss`, `h:mm:ss`, `3m20s` or seconds from the run's start (a minus is before it), or an ISO 8601 time.

```sh
curl -G "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/logs/query" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode from=02:10 --data-urlencode to=02:40 --data-urlencode stream=stdout,stderr \
  --data-urlencode 'grep=error|timeout'
```

It answers `lines` (each with `t`, its milliseconds from the start, `clock` as `mm:ss.s`, `at`, `stream` and `text`),
`matched` and `next`: up to `limit` lines (200 by default, at most 1,000), and `next` to pass as `after` while more
match. `grep` is case-insensitive text; `a|b` matches either. The `input` stream holds the clicks, scrolls and typing
the platform recorded in each browser, one line per action (`browser 1: click at 640,412`). Typed text is shown, with
keys, tokens, your run's secrets and password or one-time-code fields masked. Lines come in time order across
streams. A click, drag or drop gives its point on the browser's 1280×800 display (Chrome's bar included) and, when
the platform knew the page's geometry, the same point in the page's viewport with the viewport's size:
`browser 1: click at 200,685 (viewport 200,542 of 1279x656)`. Frames and recordings show the viewport alone, so that
point lands on a frame at 200/1279 of its width and 542/656 of its height.

`GET /v1/runs/$RUN_ID/llm-calls` lists the run's model calls in order (`at`, `provider`, `model`, `status`, tokens,
`cost_micro_usd`, `latency_ms`, and `queue_ms`, how long a call to a hosted model waited for a GPU), up to `limit`
(2,000 by default) with `next` to pass as `after`. `GET /v1/runs/$RUN_ID/screen-activity` gives, per browser, the
spans during which its screen kept changing: a gap between spans is a time the screen sat still.

Runs on the public dataset (test runs and scored runs during the hackathon) keep their logs unredacted. On a
private dataset (the final run), your logs and the feed's `error` have private values masked as `[private]`.

### Frames and recordings

```sh
curl -o frame.jpg "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/frame" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"   # the latest frame
curl -o run.webm "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/video" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"    # the recording
curl -X POST "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/video/share" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"  # a link anyone can watch
curl -X DELETE "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/video/share" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"
```

A browser's screen at any time of a finished run, cut from its recording as a PNG:

```sh
curl -o at-0213.png "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/frame?t=02:13&browser=1" -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN"
```

867	            await asyncio.gather(*late_tasks, return_exceptions=True)
868	        chosen = {}
869	        for rid, task in tasks.items():
870	            if task.done() and not task.cancelled() and task.exception() is None:
871	                chosen.update(task.result())
872	        late = sorted(set(own) - set(chosen))
873	        if late:
874	            self.board.problem("select", f"no new choice in time for {late}; the ERP workers' choices are used")

46	seen on the pages, word for word for names, numbers and dates; never guess or fill in examples. Be efficient: go

52	VIEW = re.compile(r"(?:^|\n)(URL: \S*)\nTitle: ")  # the header of every page view (SiteSession.look)
53	CURRENT_VIEW = "\nCurrent view:\n"  # where the first prompt's page view starts
54	
55	
56	# Tool results the model still needs after it moves on (a list it collected, facts it extracted): they hold no page
57	# view, so they stay, up to KEEP_CHARS.
58	KEEP_RESULTS = {"search", "collect", "extract"}
59	KEEP_CHARS = 12000
60	
61	
62	def _shrink(part):
63	    """An older page view (or long tool result) cut to a one-line stub, so context stays small."""
64	    content = part.content
65	    if isinstance(part, ToolReturnPart) and part.tool_name in KEEP_RESULTS and isinstance(content, str):
66	        if len(content) <= KEEP_CHARS:
67	            return part
68	        return dataclasses.replace(part, content=content[:KEEP_CHARS] + "\n[rest removed; call it again for all]")
69	    if isinstance(part, UserPromptPart):
70	        cut = content.find(CURRENT_VIEW) if isinstance(content, str) else -1
71	        found = VIEW.search(content, cut) if cut >= 0 else None
72	        if found is None:
73	            return part
74	        return dataclasses.replace(part, content=f"{content[:cut]}\nFirst view: {found.group(1)} [removed]")
75	    if not isinstance(part, ToolReturnPart) or not isinstance(content, str) or len(content) <= 400:
76	        return part
77	    found = VIEW.search(content)
78	    if found:
79	        lead = content[:found.start()].strip().split("\n", 1)[0]  # e.g. why an action failed
80	        stub = f"{lead}\n{found.group(1)}" if lead else found.group(1)
81	        return dataclasses.replace(part, content=f"{stub}\n[older page view removed]")
82	    return dataclasses.replace(part, content=content.split("\n", 1)[0] + "\n[older result removed]")
83	
84	
85	def _forget_old_views(messages: list[ModelMessage]) -> list[ModelMessage]:
86	    """Keep the latest page view and everything after it in full; what came before shrinks to stubs.
87	
88	    The latest view is kept even when later tool calls (note, a lookup, an unchanged page) returned no view, so the
89	    model always has the page it is on in front of it.
90	    """
91	    latest = None
92	    for i, message in enumerate(messages):
93	        if isinstance(message, ModelRequest):
94	            for j, part in enumerate(message.parts):
95	                if isinstance(part, (ToolReturnPart, UserPromptPart)) and isinstance(part.content, str) \
96	                        and VIEW.search(part.content):
97	                    latest = (i, j)
98	    if latest is None:
99	        return messages
100	    # After the latest view, tools may return long texts that are no page view (several pages opened in one step):
101	    # each rode along in every later step. Only the newest stays whole; an older one keeps its page headings.
102	    long_after = [(i, j) for i, message in enumerate(messages) if isinstance(message, ModelRequest)
103	                  for j, part in enumerate(message.parts)
104	                  if (i, j) > latest and isinstance(part, ToolReturnPart) and isinstance(part.content, str)
105	                  and len(part.content) > LONG_RESULT and part.tool_name not in KEEP_RESULTS]
106	    older = set(long_after[:-1])
107	    result: list[ModelMessage] = []
108	    for i, message in enumerate(messages):
109	        if isinstance(message, ModelRequest) and (i <= latest[0] or any(a == i for a, _ in older)):
110	            parts = [_shrink(part) if (i, j) < latest else _outline(part) if (i, j) in older else part
111	                     for j, part in enumerate(message.parts)]
112	            message = dataclasses.replace(message, parts=parts)
113	        result.append(message)
114	    return result
115	
116	
117	LONG_RESULT = 1500  # characters
118	
119	
120	def _outline(part):
121	    """A long tool result that a newer one followed: its section headings ("=== ...") and what it said last."""
122	    lines = part.content.splitlines()
123	    heads = [line for line in lines if line.startswith("=== ")][:20]
124	    last = lines[-1][:600] if lines and not lines[-1].startswith("=== ") else ""
125	    stub = "\n".join(heads or lines[:1]) + "\n[texts removed: these pages are kept for the reader]"
126	    return dataclasses.replace(part, content=stub + (f"\n{last}" if last else ""))
127	
128	
129	def steps_for(base: int, deadline: float | None, *, per_step: float = 8.0, most: float = 2.0) -> int:
130	    """
131	    A step budget that grows with the time left: `base` steps at least, more while the deadline is far (one per
132	    `per_step` seconds), at most `most` x base. A worker that is getting somewhere is not cut off by a fixed count
133	    while there is time; the deadline still bounds every worker.
134	    """
135	    if deadline is None:
136	        return base
137	    return max(base, min(int(base * most), int((deadline - time.monotonic()) / per_step)))
138	
139	
140	async def run_worker(session: SiteSession, goal: str, output_type: type[T], *, context: str = "",
141	                     deadline: float | None = None, max_steps: int = 40, thinking: bool = False,
142	                     grounded: bool = True, tools: tuple = (), notes: bool = True, strong: bool = False,
143	                     loop_guard: bool = False, stop_on_loop: bool = False
144	                     ) -> tuple[T | None, dict[str, str]]:
145	    """Work `goal` on the session's website until the model returns `output_type`; None when out of time or steps.
146	
147	    `deadline` is a `time.monotonic()` value. With `grounded`, a result whose values (anything with a digit) appear
148	    on no page the worker saw goes back to the model. `tools` adds tools beyond the browser ones; `notes=False`
149	    drops note() for short lookups that should just return. The notes the model recorded are returned either way.
150	    `strong` uses llm.strong_model() when one is configured (else the default model, as given by `thinking`).
151	    `loop_guard` warns the model when a page state keeps coming back; `stop_on_loop` then ends the run (None).
152	    """
153	    deps = Deps(session=session)
154	    browser = [tool for tool in TOOLS if notes or tool.__name__ != "note"]
155	    instructions = INSTRUCTIONS if notes else INSTRUCTIONS.replace(
156	        "Record every fact you establish with note() as soon as you have it, then return the result.",
157	        "Return the result as soon as you have it.")
158	    chosen = llm.strong_model() if strong else None
159	    agent = Agent(chosen or llm.model(), output_type=output_type, deps_type=Deps, instructions=instructions,
160	                  tools=[*browser, *tools, *clef.tools()],
161	                  model_settings=llm.strong_settings() if chosen else llm.settings(thinking), retries=4,
162	                  capabilities=[ProcessHistory(_forget_old_views)])
163	    if grounded:
164	        @agent.output_validator
165	        def _seen(ctx: RunContext[Deps], output):
166	            text = output.model_dump_json() if hasattr(output, "model_dump_json") else str(output)
167	            missing = unseen_values(text, ctx.deps.session.seen + "\n" + context)
168	            if missing:
169	                session.trace.event(session.name, "output_refused", missing=missing[:10])
170	                raise ModelRetry(f"{', '.join(missing[:10])} appear on no page you have seen. Return only values "
171	                                 f"copied from pages; open them again to check.")
172	            return output
173	
174	    session.reset_loop(guard=loop_guard, stop=stop_on_loop)
175	    view = await session.look(fresh=True)
176	    prompt = f"Website: {session.name} ({session.site['url']})\n\nGoal: {goal}\n"
177	    if context:
178	        prompt += f"\nContext:\n{context}\n"
179	    prompt += f"\n{CURRENT_VIEW}{view}"
180	    started = time.monotonic()
181	    timeout = None if deadline is None else max(1.0, deadline - started)
182	    session.trace.event(session.name, "start", goal=goal)
183	    output = None
184	    usage = RunUsage()  # filled as the run goes, so a stopped run still reports what it used
185	    try:
186	        result = await asyncio.wait_for(
187	            agent.run(prompt, deps=deps, usage=usage, usage_limits=UsageLimits(request_limit=max_steps)), timeout)
188	        output = result.output
189	        session.trace.event(session.name, "done", seconds=round(time.monotonic() - started, 1),
190	                            requests=usage.requests, input_tokens=usage.input_tokens,
191	                            cached_tokens=usage.cache_read_tokens, output_tokens=usage.output_tokens,
192	                            output=repr(output)[:500])
193	    except (asyncio.TimeoutError, UsageLimitExceeded, UnexpectedModelBehavior, Stuck) as error:
194	        session.trace.event(session.name, "stopped", reason=f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:200]}",
195	                            seconds=round(time.monotonic() - started, 1), requests=usage.requests,
196	                            input_tokens=usage.input_tokens, cached_tokens=usage.cache_read_tokens,
197	                            output_tokens=usage.output_tokens)
198	    finally:
199	        session.reset_loop()  # the next worker on this tab starts without this run's loop options
200	    return output, deps.notes

220	    async def start(self, attempts: int | None = None, until: float | None = None) -> str:
221	        """
222	        Open the site's start page in a new tab, signed in. One attempt waits on its tab while the page loads (its
223	        budget grows with the attempts, ATTEMPT_SECONDS); after RACE_AFTER without a usable page a second tab in a
224	        fresh context races it, and the first usable page wins. A tab ends early on the browser's error page, when
225	        it closes, or when its page stops answering (STUCK_SECONDS). Failed attempts are retried in a fresh
226	        context after a short backoff until `until` (default: START_MARGIN before the run's deadline; `self.until`
227	        may be moved while this runs) or `attempts` attempts.
228	        """
229	        if until is not None or self.until is None:
230	            self.until = until if until is not None else self.default_until()
231	        self._start_owner = _STARTING.set(self)
232	        self.ok = False
233	        self.settled.clear()
234	        if self._old_context is None:
235	            self._old_context = self.context  # the context the session was made with
236	        began = time.monotonic()
237	        tries = 0
238	        try:
239	            while True:
240	                tries += 1
241	                end = min(time.monotonic() + _budget(tries), self.until)
242	                own = (self.context, self.scripted)
243	                fresh = await self._fresh_context() if tries > FRESH_AFTER else None
244	                if fresh is not None:
245	                    self.context, self.scripted = fresh, None
246	                try:
247	                    winner, view = await self._race(end, began)
248	                except asyncio.CancelledError:
249	                    await self._close_pages()
250	                    self.context, self.scripted = own
251	                    await _close_context(fresh)
252	                    raise
253	                except Exception as error:
254	                    self.trace.event(self.name, "start_failed", attempt=tries,
255	                                     seconds=round(time.monotonic() - began, 1),
256	                                     error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:160]}")
257	                    await self._close_pages()
258	                    self.context, self.scripted = own  # the fresh context did not help: back
259	                    await _close_context(fresh)
260	                else:
261	                    if winner is not self:
262	                        await self._adopt(winner)
263	                        await _close_context(fresh)  # this attempt's own context lost the race
264	                    self.ok = True
265	                    self.trace.event(self.name, "start_ok", attempt=tries, seconds=round(time.monotonic() - began, 1),
266	                                     fresh_context=self.context is not self._old_context, raced=winner is not self)
267	                    return view
268	                if attempts is not None and tries >= attempts:
269	                    break
270	                wait = START_BACKOFF[min(tries, len(START_BACKOFF)) - 1]
271	                if time.monotonic() + wait + MIN_ATTEMPT > self.until:
272	                    break
273	                self.trace.event(self.name, "start_retry", after=wait, attempt=tries + 1)
274	                await asyncio.sleep(wait)
275	            raise TimeoutError(f"{self.name}: the site could not be opened in {tries} attempts "
276	                               f"({round(time.monotonic() - began)} s)")
277	        finally:
278	            _STARTING.reset(self._start_owner)
279	            self._start_owner = None
280	            self.settled.set()

282	    async def _race(self, end: float, began: float) -> tuple["SiteSession", str]:
283	        """
284	        One attempt: a tab of this session, and after RACE_AFTER without a usable page a second one next to it, in a
285	        fresh context and a session of its own (nothing is given up: the first tab may still answer first). Returns
286	        the session whose tab showed a usable page first, and that page; the racer's tab and context are closed
287	        unless it won. Raises the last error when every tab failed.
288	        """
289	        tasks = {asyncio.create_task(self._attempt(end)): self}
290	        racer_context = None
291	        error: BaseException | None = None
292	        winner = None
293	        raced_at = time.monotonic() + RACE_AFTER
294	        try:
295	            while tasks:
296	                timeout = (None if racer_context is not None or raced_at == float("inf")
297	                           else max(0.0, raced_at - time.monotonic()))
298	                done, _ = await asyncio.wait(tasks, timeout=timeout, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
299	                for task in done:
300	                    contender = tasks.pop(task)
301	                    if task.exception() is None:
302	                        winner = contender
303	                        return contender, task.result()
304	                    error = task.exception()
305	                    if tasks:  # the other tab still runs: this one's failure is only traced
306	                        self.trace.event(self.name, "start_tab_failed", seconds=round(time.monotonic() - began, 1),
307	                                         raced=contender is not self,
308	                                         error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:160]}")
309	                    if contender is not self:
310	                        await contender._close_pages()
311	                if done:
312	                    continue
313	                if racer_context is None and end - time.monotonic() > MIN_ATTEMPT:
314	                    racer_context = await self._fresh_context(why="race")
315	                    if racer_context is not None:
316	                        racer = SiteSession(self.site, racer_context, self.trace)
317	                        racer.stamp = self.stamp
318	                        tasks[asyncio.create_task(racer._attempt(end))] = racer
319	                        continue
320	                raced_at = float("inf")  # no second tab (too little time, no context): wait on the first one
321	            raise error or TimeoutError("no tab")
322	        finally:
323	            for task in tasks:
324	                task.cancel()
325	            if tasks:
326	                await asyncio.wait(list(tasks), timeout=15)  # a cancel of this start itself still propagates
327	            for contender in tasks.values():
328	                if contender is not self:
329	                    await contender._close_pages()
330	            if racer_context is not None and (winner is None or winner.context is not racer_context):
331	                await _close_context(racer_context)

333	    async def _adopt(self, racer: "SiteSession") -> None:
334	        """Take over the racer's tab, context, sign-in state and view; its tab's handlers now report here."""
335	        await self._close_pages()
336	        racer._adopted_by = self
337	        self.context, self.scripted, self.pages, self.view = racer.context, racer.scripted, racer.pages, racer.view
338	        self.stamp, self.logins, self.login_at = max(self.stamp, racer.stamp), racer.logins, racer.login_at
339	        self.events.extend(racer.events)
340	        self.seen += racer.seen
341	        self.shown, self.base, self.last_url = racer.shown, racer.base, racer.last_url
342	        for url, count in racer.visits.items():
343	            self.visits[url] = self.visits.get(url, 0) + count

345	    async def _fresh_context(self, why: str = "retry") -> BrowserContext | None:
346	        """A new context of the same browser, so a broken context (a stuck connection, cookies, a hung tab) is
347	        ruled out. None when the browser cannot make one."""
348	        try:
349	            browser = self.context.browser
350	            if browser is None:
351	                return None
352	            fresh = await asyncio.wait_for(browser.new_context(viewport={"width": 1280, "height": 800}), 20)
353	        except Exception as error:
354	            self.trace.event(self.name, "helper_error", helper="fresh_context", error=str(error)[:160])
355	            return None
356	        self.trace.event(self.name, "helper", action="fresh_context", why=why)
357	        return fresh

359	    async def _close_pages(self) -> None:
360	        for page in self.pages:
361	            try:
362	                await asyncio.wait_for(page.close(), 10)
363	            except Exception:
364	                pass
365	        self.pages = []

367	    async def _attempt(self, end: float) -> str:
368	        """One tab of a start attempt: navigate, then settle and look until the page shows, the browser's error
369	        page shows, the tab closes, its page stops answering script calls, or `end`."""
370	        if self.scripted is not self.context:
371	            await self.context.add_init_script(AUTO_CLOSE_JS)
372	            self.scripted = self.context
373	        page = await self.context.new_page()
374	        self._watch(page)
375	        try:
376	            await page.goto(self.site["url"], wait_until="domcontentloaded",
377	                            timeout=max(1.0, min(GOTO_SECONDS, end - time.monotonic())) * 1000)
378	        except Exception as error:  # still loading: the request is not given up, the tab waits on
379	            self.trace.event(self.name, "start_wait", phase="goto", url=page.url[:120],
380	                             error=str(error).splitlines()[0][:120])
381	        self.logins = 0
382	        view, phase, silent = "", "goto", None
383	
384	        def waiting(now: str) -> None:  # traced once per phase, not once per check
385	            nonlocal phase
386	            if now != phase:
387	                self.trace.event(self.name, "start_wait", phase=now, url=self.page.url[:120])
388	            phase = now
389	
390	        while True:
391	            left = end - time.monotonic()
392	            self._check_alive()
393	            if left <= 1:
394	                if view:  # it shows something (a sign-in still pending): better than another tab
395	                    return view
396	                raise TimeoutError(f"still loading ({self.page.url[:80]})")
397	            answer = await self._answers()
398	            if answer != "yes":  # nothing on the tab answers: a navigation not yet committed, or a hung page
399	                committed = not self.page.url.startswith("about:")
400	                if answer == "hung" and committed:
401	                    silent = silent or time.monotonic() - PROBE_SECONDS
402	                    if time.monotonic() - silent >= STUCK_SECONDS:
403	                        raise ConnectionError(f"the page does not respond ({self.page.url[:80]})")
404	                waiting("respond" if committed else "commit")
405	                await asyncio.sleep(min(1.0, max(0.0, left - 1)))
406	                continue
407	            silent = None
408	            try:
409	                await asyncio.wait_for(self._settle(), min(SETTLE_SECONDS, left))
410	            except asyncio.TimeoutError:  # the page answers but keeps loading: look at what it shows anyway
411	                waiting("settle")
412	            self._check_alive()
413	            try:
414	                view = await asyncio.wait_for(self.look(), max(1.0, min(LOOK_SECONDS, end - time.monotonic())))
415	            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
416	                waiting("look")
417	                view = ""
418	                continue
419	            if not self.view.strip() or self.view.startswith(("(the page does not respond", "(page error")):
420	                view = ""
421	                waiting("render")
422	                await asyncio.sleep(1.0)
423	                continue
424	            if await self._login_pending():
425	                waiting("login")
426	                await asyncio.sleep(2.0)
427	                continue
428	            return view

430	    async def _answers(self, page: Page | None = None) -> str:
431	        """Whether the page (default: the tab's) answers a script call: "yes", "hung" (no answer within
432	        PROBE_SECONDS; e.g. a navigation that never commits, or a hung page) or "error" (e.g. it navigated)."""
433	        try:
434	            await asyncio.wait_for((page or self.page).evaluate("document.readyState"), PROBE_SECONDS)
435	            return "yes"
436	        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
437	            return "hung"
438	        except Exception:
439	            return "error"

441	    async def _wait_answer(self, page: Page) -> bool:
442	        """Wait up to STUCK_SECONDS for the page to answer a script call (a navigation still committing)."""
443	        until = time.monotonic() + STUCK_SECONDS
444	        while True:
445	            answer = await self._answers(page)
446	            if answer == "yes":
447	                return True
448	            if time.monotonic() >= until or page.is_closed():
449	                return False
450	            if answer == "error":
451	                await asyncio.sleep(0.5)

454	        """Raise when the attempt's tab is provably dead: closed, or the browser's own error page."""

456	        if not open_pages:

489	    async def revive(self) -> None:
490	        """A session whose tabs are all gone (e.g. after a failed start) gets a fresh tab on the site's start page,
491	        so looking and acting never fail on an empty tab list. While a start runs in another task, this waits for
492	        it (its tab is the one to use), so a session can be handed out before it is up."""
493	        if self.starting and _STARTING.get() is not self:
494	            self.trace.event(self.name, "helper", action="wait_for_start")
495	            await self.settled.wait()
496	        if any(not page.is_closed() for page in self.pages):
497	            return
498	        page = await self.context.new_page()
499	        self._watch(page)
500	        self.events.append("the tab was gone; opened the website again")
501	        self.trace.event(self.name, "helper", action="revive")
502	        await self._goto(self.site["url"])

504	    async def _goto(self, url: str) -> None:
505	        """Open `url` in the tab and settle: at most GOTO_SECONDS plus SETTLE_SECONDS; slow ones are traced."""
506	        began = time.monotonic()
507	        try:
508	            await self.page.goto(url, wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=GOTO_SECONDS * 1000)
509	        except Exception as error:  # a slow load event still leaves a usable page
510	            first = str(error).splitlines()[0][:160]
511	            self.events.append(f"navigation was slow or failed: {first}")
512	            self.trace.event(self.name, "slow_page", phase="goto", url=url[:120],
513	                             seconds=round(time.monotonic() - began, 1), error=first)
514	        loaded = time.monotonic()
515	        await self.settle()
516	        if time.monotonic() - began > SLOW_PAGE:
517	            self.trace.event(self.name, "slow_page", phase="done", url=url[:120],
518	                             goto=round(loaded - began, 1), settle=round(time.monotonic() - loaded, 1))

520	    async def settle(self) -> None:
521	        """Let the page finish and run the generic helpers, but never longer than SETTLE_SECONDS: a click that never
522	        returns (seen on a cookie notice) must not block the tab for minutes."""
523	        try:
524	            await asyncio.wait_for(self._settle_fresh(), SETTLE_SECONDS)
525	        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
526	            self.events.append("the page kept loading; continuing with what it shows")
527	            self.trace.event(self.name, "helper_error", helper="settle", error=f"timeout after {SETTLE_SECONDS} s")
528	
529	    async def _settle_fresh(self) -> None:
530	        self.logins = 0  # a timeout later in the run may need a fresh sign-in
531	        await self._settle()

533	    async def _settle(self) -> None:
534	        page = self.page
535	        for _ in range(6):
536	            try:
537	                await page.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded", timeout=15000)
538	                await page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle", timeout=2500)
539	            except Exception:
540	                pass
541	            if not await self._wait_answer(page):  # its helpers would hang on every page call
542	                self.trace.event(self.name, "helper_error", helper="settle",
543	                                 error=f"the page answers no script call ({page.url[:80]})")
544	                return
545	            if (await self._safely(self._login, page) or await self._safely(self._cookies, page)
546	                    or await self._safely(self._error_page, page) or await self._safely(self._human_check, page)):
547	                page = self.page

552	    async def _safely(self, helper, page: Page) -> bool:
553	        """A helper that fails (a slow page, a detached element) just did nothing; the model sees the page as is. A
554	        helper never takes longer than HELPER_SECONDS: page calls on a page that stops answering wait for ever."""
555	        try:
556	            return await asyncio.wait_for(helper(page), HELPER_SECONDS)
557	        except Exception as error:
558	            text = (str(error).splitlines() or [""])[0][:160] or f"{type(error).__name__} after {HELPER_SECONDS} s"
559	            self.trace.event(self.name, "helper_error", helper=helper.__name__, error=text)
560	            return False

562	    async def _login(self, page: Page) -> bool:
563	        password = page.locator("input[type=password]:visible")
564	        if not await password.count() or self.logins >= 2:
565	            return False
566	        if self.login_at and self.login_at[1] == page.url and time.monotonic() - self.login_at[0] < LOGIN_PATIENCE:
567	            return False  # sent moments ago and the old page still shows: the post is pending, do not resend it
568	        self.logins += 1
569	        form = password.first.locator("xpath=ancestor::form[1]")
570	        scope = form if await form.count() else page.locator("body")
571	        user = scope.locator("input:visible:not([type=password]):not([type=hidden]):not([type=checkbox])"
572	                             ":not([type=radio]):not([type=submit]):not([type=button])")
573	        if not await user.count():
574	            return False
575	        creds = self.site["credentials"]
576	        await user.first.fill(creds["username"])
577	        await password.first.fill(creds["password"])
578	        try:
579	            await password.first.press("Enter", timeout=5000)
580	        except Exception:
581	            pass  # the form was sent; the page is still loading, which settle waits for
582	        self.login_at = (time.monotonic(), page.url)
583	        self.events.append("signed in with this run's login")
584	        self.trace.event(self.name, "helper", action="login", url=page.url)
585	        await asyncio.sleep(0.3)
586	        return True

588	    async def _cookies(self, page: Page) -> bool:
589	        buttons = page.locator("button:visible, input[type=submit]:visible")
590	        candidates = []
591	        for i in range(min(await buttons.count(), 20)):
592	            button = buttons.nth(i)
593	            text = (await button.inner_text() if await button.evaluate("e => e.tagName") == "BUTTON"
594	                    else await button.get_attribute("value")) or ""

596	                candidates.append((not COOKIE_MINIMAL.search(text), text.strip(), button))
597	        if not candidates:
598	            return False
599	        candidates.sort(key=lambda c: c[0])  # the necessary-only choice first
600	        _, text, button = candidates[0]

9	circles are warned and (in the race) stopped, the bid form gets more time, and a bid without positions
10	still carries the discount. See docs/changes-v3.md for the changes and the environment variables.

37	def warm_up(sessions: dict[str, SiteSession], deadline: float, critical: set[str]) -> dict[str, asyncio.Task]:
38	    """
39	    Start signing in to every website in the background and return at once: nothing waits for all of them. The
40	    `critical` ones (the bid website, the mailbox) keep retrying until START_MARGIN before the deadline; the others
41	    give up after RESEARCH_START_SECONDS. A session whose start is still running can be handed out: its first look
42	    waits for the start (SiteSession.revive).
43	    """
44	    browser_tools.DEADLINE = deadline
45	    tasks = {}
46	    for name, session in sessions.items():
47	        limit = deadline - browser_tools.START_MARGIN
48	        if name not in critical:
49	            limit = min(limit, time.monotonic() + RESEARCH_START_SECONDS)
50	        session.until = limit
51	        tasks[name] = asyncio.create_task(session.start(until=limit), name=f"start@{name}")
52	        tasks[name].add_done_callback(lambda t: t.cancelled() or t.exception())  # failures are traced in start
53	    return tasks

56	async def solve(task: dict, page, answer: dict | None = None,
57	                attributes: dict[str, dict[str, str]] | None = None) -> dict | None:
58	    """
59	    Enter the bid on the run's website (a "site" submission) and return None.
60	
61	    `answer` (calc's BidResult.answer()) and `attributes` (per position, the chosen material's attributes) are what
62	    the bid worker enters; positions they do not give completely are omitted. Unless given, the orchestrator
63	    researches them; a research failure never costs the signed bid.
64	    """
65	    trace = Trace()
66	    loopwatch.Watchdog(activity=lambda: trace.last).start()  # a blocked loop or a silent run dumps its stacks
67	    left = min(contract.seconds_left(task), LOCAL_SECONDS)
68	    deadline = time.monotonic() + left - SAFETY_SECONDS
69	    # Sign in to every website in the background: the brief, the planner and the workers never wait for all of
70	    # them. The bid website (named by the run contract) keeps warming; the mailbox too, once the brief names it.
71	    contexts = await browsers.more_contexts(page, len(task["access"]))
72	    sessions = {site["siteId"]: SiteSession(site, context, trace) for site, context in zip(task["access"], contexts)}
73	    contract_site = (task.get("submission") or {}).get("siteId")
74	    starts = warm_up(sessions, deadline, {contract_site} if contract_site in sessions else set(sessions))
75	    briefing = await read_brief(task)
76	    # The run contract names the submission website; it wins over the model's reading of the brief.
77	    if contract_site in sessions and contract_site != briefing.bid_site:
78	        trace.event("briefing", "bid_site_corrected", read=briefing.bid_site, contract=contract_site)
79	        briefing = briefing.model_copy(update={"bid_site": contract_site})
80	    trace.event("briefing", "done", **briefing.model_dump(exclude={"submission_steps"}))

"""A run's trace: one JSON line per event in a file, and a short line on stdout for the run logs."""
import json
import os
import time
from pathlib import Path


CURRENT: "Trace | None" = None  # the run's trace, for the summary at the very end


def print_summary() -> None:
    """The current run's phase and failure events in one block (no-op before a trace exists)."""
    if CURRENT is not None:
        CURRENT.summary()


class Trace:
    def __init__(self, directory: str | None = None):
        global CURRENT
        CURRENT = self
        self.key: list[str] = []
        self.started = self.last = time.monotonic()
        directory = directory or os.environ.get("TRACE_DIR", "traces")
        Path(directory).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.path = Path(directory) / time.strftime("run-%Y%m%d-%H%M%S.jsonl")
        self.file = self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8")

    # events that mark a phase or a failure; repeated in one block at the end of the run (summary())
    KEY_KINDS = {"start", "done", "stopped", "problem", "start_failed", "spec_done", "tender_facts", "mail_kind",
                 "answer", "summary_check", "last_chance", "crashed", "decision_disputed", "helper_error"}

    def event(self, worker: str, kind: str, quiet: bool = False, **data) -> None:
        self.last = time.monotonic()
        seconds = round(self.last - self.started, 2)
        self.file.write(json.dumps({"t": seconds, "worker": worker, "kind": kind, **data}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
        self.file.flush()
        if quiet:  # file only, e.g. the full page views
            return
        brief = " ".join(f"{k}={str(v)[:120]!r}" if isinstance(v, str) else f"{k}={v}" for k, v in data.items())
        print(f"[{seconds:7.1f}s] {worker:<15} {kind:<12} {brief}", flush=True)
        if kind in self.KEY_KINDS:
            self.key.append(f"[{seconds:7.1f}s] {worker:<15} {kind:<12} {brief[:150]}")

    def summary(self, limit: int = 120) -> None:
        """Print the phase and failure events again in one block: the platform keeps only the last few hundred
        lines of a run's output, so without this the early phases are missing from every run log."""
        lines = self.key if len(self.key) <= limit else self.key[:20] + ["  ..."] + self.key[-(limit - 21):]
        print("===== run summary =====\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n===== end of run summary =====", flush=True)

1	"""
2	The model behind the workers: the hosted Qwen through the run's metering proxy by default.
3	
4	AGENT_MODEL picks another model on the same OpenAI-compatible endpoint (QWEN_BASE_URL). Thinking is off for
5	navigation steps, which makes a step about three times faster, and on where a worker has to weigh evidence.
6	
7	Timeouts are per mode, because the hosted model now and then hangs a call for minutes until the proxy drops it: a
8	thinking-off step answers in 2 to 5 s, so it gets a short timeout and a quick retry (LLM_TIMEOUT, 45 s, which
9	leaves room for the 30 to 36 s calls a longer answer takes); a thinking-on call legitimately takes 25 to 45 s, so it
10	gets a long one (LLM_TIMEOUT_THINKING, 90 s). Time grows with the answer: copying 80 table rows took 85 s even
11	without thinking. `settings(thinking)` carries the right timeout in the ModelSettings; pydantic-ai passes it to
12	the OpenAI client per request, so one client serves both modes. A call known to run longer (a reader writing a long
13	typed answer) passes `settings(thinking, timeout=seconds)`; that per-request value beats any timeout set on the
14	client. LLM_RETRIES attempts follow each failure with a short backoff (0.5 s doubling, capped at 8 s).
15	
16	The timeout bounds the whole call, not each read: while the model works, the proxy sends the headers and then a
17	newline every few seconds, so a plain read timeout never fires and a hung call would run until the proxy gives up.
18	
19	LLM_STREAM_WATCHDOG=1 swaps the whole-call deadline for progress checks (see `_WatchdogModel`): each call is
20	streamed, a call whose first chunk does not arrive within LLM_FIRST_TOKEN_TIMEOUT (20 s) is retried, and a call
21	that is answering may run on as long as it keeps making progress, up to LLM_MAX_CALL (300 s). The proxy streams
22	text and reasoning token by token but holds back tool-call arguments until they are complete, so a request with
23	tools may stay silent after its last token for as long as its timeout above; one without tools may pause
24	LLM_IDLE_TIMEOUT (15 s). LLM_HEDGE_AFTER sends a second copy of a call that has not started after that many
25	seconds and keeps whichever starts first (the losing copy may still be billed).
26	
27	LLM_BACKEND=anthropic runs the same agents on a Claude model with the team's own key instead (LLM_MODEL, default
28	claude-haiku-5-5; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, a team secret in test and scored runs). Its calls go through the run's metering
29	proxy too: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, which the platform sets to $LLM_PROXY_URL/anthropic. Without a key the run falls back
30	to the hosted Qwen. Thinking off maps to Anthropic's thinking off (or the closest the model allows), thinking on to
31	adaptive thinking at LLM_EFFORT (default medium); see `anthropic_thinking`. The per-mode deadlines, the retries and
32	the call log are the same; the stream watchdog is Qwen-only (Claude calls do not hang the way the hosted model does).

120	class _Limits:
121	    def __init__(self, *, first: float, idle: float, silence: float, tools: bool) -> None:

132	    """Whether a stream chunk carries model output (text, reasoning or a tool call), not just a role or usage."""
133	    for choice in getattr(chunk, "choices", None) or ():

137	        extra = delta.model_extra or {}
138	        if delta.content or delta.tool_calls or extra.get("reasoning_content") or extra.get("reasoning"):

143	class _WatchedStream:
144	    """An OpenAI chunk stream that raises Stalled when the call goes quiet for longer than its limits allow.
145	    The proxy's keep-alive comments never reach here (the SSE decoder drops them), so they do not count."""
146	
147	    def __init__(self, stream, limits: _Limits) -> None:
148	        self._stream, self._limits = stream, limits
149	        self._chunks = 0
150	        self._last = time.monotonic()
151	
152	    def _wait(self) -> float:
153	        quiet = self._limits.first if not self._chunks else self._limits.quiet
154	        return max(self._last + quiet - time.monotonic(), 0.0)
155	
156	    async def __aiter__(self):
157	        source = self._stream.__aiter__()
158	        while True:
159	            try:
160	                chunk = await asyncio.wait_for(anext(source), self._wait())
161	            except StopAsyncIteration:
162	                return
163	            except TimeoutError:
164	                if not self._chunks:
165	                    raise Stalled(f"no first chunk within {self._limits.first:g}s") from None
166	                raise Stalled(f"no progress for {self._limits.quiet:g}s after {self._chunks} chunks") from None
167	            if not self._chunks or _progress(chunk):
168	                self._last = time.monotonic()
169	            self._chunks += 1
170	            yield chunk

172	    async def __aenter__(self):
173	        await self._stream.__aenter__()
174	        return self

176	    async def __aexit__(self, *exc) -> None:
177	        await self._stream.__aexit__(*exc)

179	    async def close(self) -> None:

182	    def __getattr__(self, name):
183	        return getattr(self._stream, name)

186	class _WatchdogModel(OpenAIChatModel):
187	    """The OpenAI chat model; with LLM_STREAM_WATCHDOG on, a request is streamed under progress limits, retried when
188	    it stalls, and handed back as one ModelResponse, so agents run unchanged."""
189	
190	    async def _completions_create(self, messages, stream, model_settings, model_request_parameters):
191	        response = await super()._completions_create(messages, stream, model_settings, model_request_parameters)
192	        limits = _WATCH.get()
193	        if stream and limits is not None and not isinstance(response, ModelResponse):
194	            return _WatchedStream(response, limits)
195	        return response

197	    async def request(self, messages: list[ModelMessage], model_settings: ModelSettings | None,
198	                      model_request_parameters: ModelRequestParameters) -> ModelResponse:
199	        if not watchdog():
200	            return await super().request(messages, model_settings, model_request_parameters)
201	        settings = ModelSettings(**(model_settings or {}))
202	        thinking = bool(((settings.get("extra_body") or {}).get("chat_template_kwargs") or {}).get("enable_thinking"))
203	        silence = float(settings.get("timeout") or timeout_seconds(thinking))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
204	        cap = env_seconds("LLM_MAX_CALL", DEFAULT_MAX_CALL)
205	        settings["timeout"] = cap  # the HTTP layer only guards the cap; progress is judged here
206	        tools = bool(model_request_parameters.function_tools or model_request_parameters.output_tools)
207	        limits = _Limits(first=env_seconds("LLM_FIRST_TOKEN_TIMEOUT", DEFAULT_FIRST_TOKEN),
208	                         idle=env_seconds("LLM_IDLE_TIMEOUT", DEFAULT_IDLE), silence=silence, tools=tools)
209	        attempts = retries() + 1
210	        for attempt in range(1, attempts + 1):
211	            token = _WATCH.set(limits)
212	            try:
213	                async with asyncio.timeout(cap):
214	                    return await self._attempt(messages, settings, model_request_parameters, limits)
215	            except (Stalled, TimeoutError, httpx2.TransportError) as error:
216	                reason = str(error) or f"no answer within {cap:g}s"
217	            except ModelAPIError as error:
218	                if isinstance(error, ModelHTTPError) and error.status_code < 500 and error.status_code != 429:
219	                    raise
220	                reason = str(error)
221	            finally:
222	                _WATCH.reset(token)
223	            if attempt == attempts:
224	                raise ModelAPIError(self.model_name, f"model call failed {attempts} times; last: {reason}")
225	            print(f"[model] stalled thinking {'on' if thinking else 'off'}: {reason}; retry {attempt}/{attempts - 1}",
226	                  flush=True)
227	            await asyncio.sleep(_backoff(attempt))
228	        raise AssertionError("unreachable")

230	    async def _attempt(self, messages, settings, params, limits: _Limits) -> ModelResponse:
231	        """One streamed call (two when hedging): wait for the first chunk, then read the stream to its end."""
232	        async with AsyncExitStack() as stack:
233	            streamed = await self._start(stack, messages, settings, params, limits)
234	            async for _ in streamed:
235	                pass
236	            return streamed.get()

238	    async def _open(self, messages, settings, params):
239	        stack = AsyncExitStack()
240	        try:
241	            streamed = await stack.enter_async_context(self.request_stream(messages, settings, params))
242	        except BaseException:
243	            await stack.aclose()
244	            raise
245	        return stack, streamed

247	    async def _start(self, stack: AsyncExitStack, messages, settings, params, limits: _Limits):
248	        """Open the stream (request_stream returns once the first chunk is in). With LLM_HEDGE_AFTER, a second copy
249	        goes out when the first has not started by then; the first copy to start wins, the other is dropped."""
250	        hedge = hedge_seconds()
251	        tasks = [asyncio.create_task(self._open(messages, settings, params))]
252	        first_copy = tasks[0]
253	        deadline = time.monotonic() + limits.first
254	        hedged = False
255	        try:
256	            if 0 < hedge < limits.first:
257	                done, _ = await asyncio.wait(tasks, timeout=hedge)
258	                if not done:
259	                    print(f"[model] no first chunk after {hedge:g}s: sending a hedge copy", flush=True)
260	                    tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(self._open(messages, settings, params)))
261	                    deadline = time.monotonic() + limits.first
262	                    hedged = True
263	            while tasks:
264	                done, _ = await asyncio.wait(tasks, timeout=max(deadline - time.monotonic(), 0),
265	                                             return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
266	                if not done:
267	                    raise Stalled(f"no first chunk within {limits.first:g}s")
268	                for task in done:
269	                    tasks.remove(task)
270	                    if task.exception() is None:
271	                        inner, streamed = task.result()
272	                        stack.push_async_callback(inner.aclose)
273	                        if hedged:
274	                            print(f"[model] hedge: the {'first' if task is first_copy else 'hedge'} copy "
275	                                  "started first and is kept", flush=True)
276	                        return streamed
277	                    if not tasks:
278	                        raise task.exception()  # type: ignore[misc]
279	            raise AssertionError("unreachable")
280	        finally:
281	            for task in tasks:  # copies that lost the race or never started
282	                task.cancel()
283	            for result in await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True):
284	                if isinstance(result, tuple):
285	                    await result[0].aclose()

351	    """An HTTP client whose read timeout is a deadline for the whole call (headers and body), so the proxy's

354	    async def send(self, request: httpx2.Request, *, stream: bool = False, **kwargs) -> httpx2.Response:
355	        seconds = (request.extensions.get("timeout") or {}).get("read")
356	        if not seconds:

358	        deadline = time.monotonic() + seconds

361	        except TimeoutError:

363	        if stream:

"""
Make a hung run diagnosable: a daemon thread watches a heartbeat the event loop updates every second.

When the loop has not beaten for STALE_SECONDS (synchronous work or a blocking call on the loop), every thread's
stack goes to stdout once (faulthandler, so it lands in the run log), at most every REPEAT_SECONDS. When the loop
still runs but the trace has been silent for SILENT_SECONDS (every task waiting on something that never comes),
the stacks of all asyncio tasks go to stdout instead.
"""
import asyncio
import faulthandler
import sys
import threading
import time

STALE_SECONDS = 20.0
REPEAT_SECONDS = 60.0
SILENT_SECONDS = 300.0


class Watchdog:
    def __init__(self, activity=None, stale: float = STALE_SECONDS, repeat: float = REPEAT_SECONDS,
                 silent: float = SILENT_SECONDS, out=None):
        self.activity = activity  # a callable: time.monotonic() of the run's latest trace event
        self.stale, self.repeat, self.silent = stale, repeat, silent
        self.out = out or sys.stdout
        self.beat = time.monotonic()
        self.dumps = 0
        self._stop = threading.Event()
        self._task: asyncio.Task | None = None

    def start(self) -> "Watchdog":
        self._task = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task(self._heartbeat(), name="watchdog")
        threading.Thread(target=self._watch, name="loop-watchdog", daemon=True).start()
        return self

    def stop(self) -> None:
        self._stop.set()
        if self._task is not None:
            self._task.cancel()

    async def _heartbeat(self) -> None:
        last_tasks_dump = 0.0
        while True:
            self.beat = time.monotonic()
            if self.activity is not None:
                quiet = self.beat - self.activity()
                if quiet > self.silent and self.beat - last_tasks_dump > self.silent:
                    last_tasks_dump = self.beat
                    self._dump_tasks(quiet)
            await asyncio.sleep(1.0)

    def _dump_tasks(self, quiet: float) -> None:
        tasks = [t for t in asyncio.all_tasks() if t is not self._task]
        print(f"[watchdog] no trace event for {quiet:.0f} s; stacks of {len(tasks)} asyncio tasks follow",
              file=self.out, flush=True)
        for task in tasks:
            try:
                task.print_stack(limit=12, file=self.out)
            except Exception as error:
                print(f"[watchdog] {task.get_name()}: {error}", file=self.out)
        self.out.flush()

    def _watch(self) -> None:
        last_dump = 0.0
        while not self._stop.wait(1.0):
            now = time.monotonic()
            blocked = now - self.beat
            if blocked > self.stale and now - last_dump > self.repeat:
                last_dump = now
                self.dumps += 1
                try:
                    print(f"[watchdog] the event loop has not run for {blocked:.0f} s; thread stacks follow",
                          file=self.out, flush=True)
                    faulthandler.dump_traceback(file=self.out, all_threads=True)
                    self.out.flush()
                except Exception:
                    pass

The run wasn't slow because of tokens: it hung. Two ERP tabs stopped answering at about 150 s, and from 167 s until you cancelled at 494 s there was no model call and no log line at all. I've fixed the hang; the fixes pass the unit tests but have not been through a sandbox run yet, and nothing is committed.

## Why it got stuck

All the research except the ERP was finished by 125 s (tender facts at 99 s, every mail kind visible in the log by 125 s). Then nothing bounded the wait on the two hung tabs:

- **Sign-in check with no timeout:** after a page stops answering, `open_pages` asks "is this a sign-in form?" with a `locator.count()` that never returns (`agent/research.py:1012`).
- **Tab start waited on forever:** once the racing tab had failed, a start whose `new_page()` never returned was awaited with no limit (`agent/browser_tools.py:295`).
- **No per-material budget:** a material worker's deadline was the whole research deadline, so one material that normally takes 15–60 s could sit for about 10 minutes.

This is the same failure as the earlier 880 s run (`run_a43d633bb7a2baca`): one material sat for 590 s, its requirement got no record, and the bid became a wrong `no_bid` (quality 5). So it costs quality as well as time.

## What I changed

- Every one of those browser calls now has a timeout.
- A start gives up shortly after its time budget instead of waiting on a tab that never opens.
- An ERP tab that stops answering is replaced by a new tab that opens the same address again. This applies only to ERP tabs, never the bid form.
- A dead tab is no longer handed to the next worker.
- One search or one material attempt gets at most 90 s (the existing `MATERIAL_SECONDS`), then the existing second attempt runs.

None of this depends on site names, paths or values. I added tests in `agent/tests/test_hang.py` and a note in `docs/learned.md`. I did not start a sandbox run because the team already had five test runs in flight; when a slot is free:

```sh
dev/test-run.sh v2 "bounded ERP tab waits, hung tab replaced, per-material budget" hang-fix
```

## Cache reads and writes

Cache reads are there: 289,952 of the 851,818 prompt tokens in this run (34%), and 32–37% in the four other runs I checked. Cache writes are always 0 for the hosted Qwen, because its cache is implicit and the platform prices writes as free. `experiments/runs.jsonl` shows `null` tokens only because `dev/track.py` never fetches the per-call list (`/v1/runs/<id>/llm-calls`).

## Where the tokens go

A full run uses about 1.0–1.2M prompt tokens ($0.13–0.15), and 85–90% of that is spent in the first ~170 s of research. Your last token cut worked: 0.85M for this run's research against 0.85–1.12M in the same window of four earlier runs.

| Part | Share of prompt tokens |
| --- | --- |
| Mail searches (nine kinds, each its own browsing worker) | about a third (estimate) |
| ERP (searches, material views, readers) | about 30% (estimate) |
| Bid form and signing | 7–8% |
| Specification | 6–7% |
| Tender Q&A | 3–4% |
| Readers, verifier, plan, choices | the rest |

The mail and ERP shares are estimates, because workers that are stopped early don't log their tokens. Cost is only a tie-breaker after quality, and the time goes to waiting, not to tokens.

## Tender and webmail: what still needs a push

I did not change these; each is generic and should be measured with a test run before it stays.

- **Model calls that never start:** each one costs 20 s until the watchdog retries. In one good run, 5 of them fell in the form and signing phase, about 100 of its 206 s. `LLM_HEDGE_AFTER` already exists and is off; trying it at about 8 s is the cheapest next experiment.
- **Bid form pages that don't settle:** in `run_9f7e27eb577743c3`, three consecutive steps each waited about 47 s, which looks like the 45 s settle cap; the form took 232 s there against 71 s in the best run. A fix is riskier here because a reload can lose unsaved form steps.
- **TAN worker:** it hit its 10-step limit in 2 of 5 runs (22 s and 105 s lost), paging back and forth before a second attempt found the mail by search. Turning on the existing loop guard for it, or a few more steps, would help.
- **Silence watchdog:** it only dumps stacks after 300 s of silence, and none showed in this run's log before the cancel at 494 s. Around 90 s would have shown this hang in the log directly.

class Fake:
    """The proxy: answers the n-th call with the n-th script (headers after `headers` seconds; None = never)."""

    def __init__(self, *calls: tuple[float | None, list[tuple[float, bytes]]]) -> None:
        self.calls = list(calls)
        self.count = 0

    async def handler(self, request: httpx2.Request) -> httpx2.Response:
        headers, pieces = self.calls[min(self.count, len(self.calls) - 1)]
        self.count += 1
        if headers is None:
            await asyncio.sleep(3600)
        await asyncio.sleep(headers)
        return httpx2.Response(200, headers={"content-type": "text/event-stream"}, stream=Script(pieces))

def run(fake: Fake, *, tools: bool = False, **env: str):
    """One model request through the watchdog; returns the response, the seconds it took and the log."""
    async def go():
        http = llm._DeadlineClient(transport=httpx2.MockTransport(fake.handler))
        client = AsyncOpenAI(base_url="http://models.example/v1", api_key="k", max_retries=0, http_client=http)
        model = llm._WatchdogModel("m", provider=OpenAIProvider(openai_client=client))
        params = ModelRequestParameters(output_tools=[TOOL] if tools else [], allow_text_output=not tools)
        return await model.request([ModelRequest.user_text_prompt("hi")], llm.settings(), params)

    out = io.StringIO()
    started = time.monotonic()
    with patch.dict(os.environ, {**WATCH, **env}), redirect_stdout(out):
        response = asyncio.run(go())
    return response, time.monotonic() - started, out.getvalue()


class Watchdog(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        backoff = patch.object(llm, "_backoff", lambda attempt: 0.0)

        self.assertNotIn("stalled", log)

async def _search(session: SiteSession, kind: Kind, reference: str, kept: _Reading, until: float,
                  again: bool) -> str:
    """
    One worker run; it ends at `until`, KEEP_GRACE after its first kept message (the other folders), or when the
    tab showed no new page for STALL_SECONDS (then the tab is replaced). Returns "done" (the model finished),
    "ended" (stopped by time) or "stalled".
    """
    worker = asyncio.create_task(run_worker(
        session, _goal(kind, reference, again), Summary, deadline=until, max_steps=20, thinking=True,
        grounded=False, notes=False,  # kept messages are read for the worker: no note tool, no note steps
        tools=(paging_tool(Collected()), keep_messages_tool(kept), keep_open_tool(kept))))
    stalled, ended = False, False
    progress, moved = (session.stamp, len(kept)), time.monotonic()
    try:
        while not worker.done():
            now = time.monotonic()
            if (session.stamp, len(kept)) != progress or kept.opening:
                progress, moved = (session.stamp, len(kept)), now
            stop = until if kept.first is None else min(until, kept.first + KEEP_GRACE)
            stalled = now - moved >= STALL_SECONDS
            if now >= stop or stalled:
                reason = ("no page view for a while" if stalled
                          else "grace after the first hit" if kept.first else "budget")
                session.trace.event(session.name, "mail_search_ended", record_kind=kind.name, kept=len(kept),
                                    reason=reason)
                ended = True
                break
            await asyncio.wait({worker}, timeout=min(2.0, max(0.1, stop - now)))
    finally:
        worker.cancel()  # also when the caller is cancelled at the mail deadline
    try:
        await worker
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        if not worker.cancelled():
            raise
    except Exception as error:  # what was kept so far still counts
        session.trace.event(session.name, "mail_search_failed", record_kind=kind.name,
                            error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:160]}")
    if stalled:
        await _fresh_tab(session)
        return "stalled"
    if ended or worker.cancelled() or worker.exception() is not None or worker.result()[0] is None:
        return "ended"
    return "done"


async def _fresh_tab(session: SiteSession) -> None:
    """A tab that stopped answering (a hung page or sign-in under load) is replaced by a new one on the website."""
    for page in session.pages:
        try:
            await asyncio.wait_for(page.close(), 10)
        except Exception:
            pass
    session.pages = []
    try:
        await asyncio.wait_for(session.revive(), 60)
    except Exception as error:
        session.trace.event(session.name, "helper_error", helper="fresh_tab", error=str(error)[:160])

async def _select_state(element) -> dict:
    return await element.evaluate(
        "e => ({disabled: e.disabled, options: Array.from(e.options).map(o => ({value: o.value, "
        "text: (o.textContent || '').trim(), selected: o.selected, disabled: o.disabled}))})")


async def _confirm(session, plan: FillPlan, view: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
    """Click the button the model named as the confirm of a choice; the new view, or the old one and an error."""
    button, why = find_control(view, plan.confirm, ("button",))
    target = await locate(session.page, button) if button else None
    if target is None:
        return view, why or f"{plan.confirm!r} vanished from the page"
    await target.click(timeout=5000)
    await session.settle()
    return await session.look(), None


async def fill_position(session, entry: dict, plan: FillPlan, log: list[str],
                        choices: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> str | None:
    """
    Enter one position's values into the form on screen, control by control in page order; returns an error
    message, or None when every mapped control holds its value.

    A select mapped to a material attribute (a key that is not an answer field) is a choice that narrows the next
    one: after setting it, `plan.confirm` is clicked so the page offers the next level, and the choice must survive
    that round trip. A control still disabled (a choice from an earlier visit not yet confirmed) gets one confirm.
    `choices` (label -> option text) is the model's pick for such a choice, used only where a worded attribute
    matches no option literally; numbers must match exactly, and answer fields are never overridden.
    """
    picked = {clean(label): text for label, text in (choices or {}).items()}
    answer_keys = MONEY_KEYS | COUNT_KEYS | {"material_number", "position"}
    # a position counts as entered only with its material, quantity, price and lead time (the material control
    # opens only once the choices before it are made)
    unmapped = sorted(set(REQUIRED_KEYS) - {"position"} - set(plan.fields.values()))
    if unmapped:
        return f"no control mapped for {', '.join(unmapped)}: add them to fields"
    view = await session.look()
    order = {clean(label): i for i, (_, _, label) in enumerate(controls(view))}
    mapping = sorted(plan.fields.items(), key=lambda item: order.get(clean(item[0]), len(order)))
    for label, key in mapping:
        if key not in entry:
            log.append(f"{label}: left empty (this bid gives no value for it, which is fine)")
            continue
        value = form_value(key, entry[key])
        for attempt in range(2):
            ref, why = find_control(view, label, ("select", "textbox", "textarea"))
            element = await locate(session.page, ref) if ref else None
            if element is None and ref is None and key not in REQUIRED_KEYS:
                # a label the model guessed for a value the form has no control for (live: "Druck" for the
                # pressure, which the form shows only inside the catalogue option): skip it, never fail the
                # position over it; the required values still need their controls
                break
            if element is None:
                return why or f"{label!r} vanished from the page"
            if not await element.evaluate("e => e.disabled || e.readOnly === true"):
                break
            if attempt or not plan.confirm:
                return (f"{label!r} is disabled: an earlier choice was not confirmed or leads elsewhere "
                        f"(check the values chosen so far)")
            # a choice made on an earlier visit may still wait for its confirm
            view, error = await _confirm(session, plan, view)
            if error:
                return error
        if element is None:
            log.append(f"{label}: no such control on this page; skipped")
            continue
        if await element.evaluate("e => e.tagName") == "SELECT":
            state = await _select_state(element)
            option, why = match_option(state["options"], value)
            if option is None and key not in answer_keys and clean(label) in picked and parse_number(value) is None:
                option, why = match_option(state["options"], picked[clean(label)])  # the model's reading
            if option is None:
                shown = " | ".join(o["text"] for o in state["options"] if o["value"])[:600]
                worded = key not in answer_keys and parse_number(value) is None
                hint = (f" If one option means the same as {value!r}, call again with choices={{{label!r}: <that "
                        f"option>}}." if worded else " A number must match exactly: leave this position out.")
                return f"{label!r}: {why}. Options: {shown}.{hint}"
            changed = not option.get("selected")
            if changed:
                await element.select_option(value=option["value"], timeout=5000)
            log.append(f"{label} = {option['text']}")
            if key in answer_keys or not plan.confirm or not changed:
                continue
            view, error = await _confirm(session, plan, view)
            if error:
                return error
            ref, _ = find_control(view, label, ("select",))
            kept = await locate(session.page, ref) if ref else None
            if kept is None or await kept.evaluate("e => e.value") != option["value"]:
                return f"{label!r} lost its choice after {plan.confirm!r}"
        else:
            problem = await type_value(element, value, numeric=key in MONEY_KEYS | COUNT_KEYS)
            if problem:
                return f"{label!r} {problem}"
            log.append(f"{label} = {value}")
    return None

async def type_value(element, value: str, numeric: bool) -> str | None:
    """
    Type a value into a field and check that the field holds it; None when it does, else what went wrong. A
    number is tried in the notation of the answer first (decimal comma), then with a decimal point and no
    thousands separator, which a number field or an English form wants; and the check compares numbers as numbers,
    since a field may show what it took in its own way ("1.234,50", "1234.5").
    """
    number = parse_number(value) if numeric else None
    notations = [value]
    if number is not None and format(number, "f") not in notations:
        notations.append(format(number, "f"))
    why = ""
    for text in notations:
        try:
            await element.fill(text, timeout=5000)
        except Exception as error:  # e.g. a number field refuses a comma
            why = str(error).splitlines()[0][:120]
            continue
        held = await element.evaluate("e => e.value")
        if held == text or (number is not None and parse_number(str(held)) == number):
            return None
        why = f"it holds {held!r}"
    return f"did not take {value!r} ({why})"

No — none of them reads a site name, URL, label or value. One was calibrated to how fast the public ERP is, and I've replaced it. A third sandbox run with everything is in flight; the full unit suite passes (314 tests).

## Overfitting check, change by change

| Change | Depends on public-1? |
| --- | --- |
| Timeouts on browser calls that never returned | No. Any browser, any site. |
| ERP tab that stops answering is replaced by a new tab | No. If a private ERP keeps its sign-in per tab instead of per browser context, the new tab lands on the sign-in page and the existing sign-in helper handles it. |
| 90 s budget per ERP search or material | **Yes, this was the fitted one.** 90 s came from public materials taking 15–60 s; a slower private ERP would have been cut mid-read. Replaced. |
| Second copy of a model call after 6 s | No. It is fitted to the model service (99% of calls start within 4.1 s), not to the data, and the final uses the same hosted model. Capped at four at once. |
| TAN lookup: 16 steps and the loop warning | No. It loosens a limit that was tight for the public mailbox, so it is less fitted than before. |
| Bid form waits for a busy page | No. The wait is half of whatever time the form has left, not a number taken from a run. |

The replacement for the 90 s budget judges an ERP worker by progress: it is ended only when its tab has shown no new view of an answering page for longer than one navigation is allowed to take (the browser layer's own limits). A slow site that keeps delivering pages is never cut.

## What the second sandbox run showed

It finished in 275 s but scored 72, and the cause is the real tender problem, not one of my changes:

- The research was fully correct, with all five positions calculated.
- In the bid form the site held its answer to one choice for about 30 s. Three retries of the next click timed out within 14 s, the helper reported "failed three times", and the model omitted position 01.03.
- I've changed that rule: a click timeout now means "the page is busy", and the position is retried while time allows instead of being dropped. This is the same event that cost 150 s in the earlier slow run.

## Runs so far

| Run | Changes included | Quality | Time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `run_69f6e25bded982e1` | hang fix only | 100 | 365 s |
| `run_bb96aee9bfce88e8` | plus hedge and TAN | 72 | 275 s |
| third run (in flight) | plus progress-based ERP check and busy-page wait | pending | pending |

Neither finished run hit an ERP hang or a model call that needed a second copy, so those two fixes are covered by unit tests only so far. Nothing is committed; I'll report the third run's score when it ends.

content.text:
Technically yes, but the rules forbid the version you're describing, and it would not fix what is actually slow.

**Why not the full capture.** The platform's agent requirement says helpers "must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence", and the fair-play page lists "a crawler that grabs everything for one model call" as a rejection reason. A reviewer agent reads every package, so a crawl-first design risks losing the submission, not just points.

**Why it would not work well even if allowed:**
- **Not link-reachable:** most of the evidence sits behind searches and forms (materials by catalogue group, mail by reference, the configurator's dependent choices), so there is no fixed set of pages to download.
- **More noise:** the sites are full of look-alike, superseded and future-dated records. Grabbing everything hands the model more traps to sort out, which is where the quality points are.
- **More load, more hangs:** every extra page load is another chance to hit the held responses we just spent the session on.
- **Token cost:** raw HTML and JavaScript are several times larger than the text view the workers read now.

**What is allowed and gets most of the benefit.** The rules explicitly permit extracting a page the model selected, parsing a document it selected, and paginating a result set it selected. Three things fit inside that:

1. **Keep the raw HTML of every page a model opens** in one store shared by all workers, so nothing is fetched twice and readers can re-read without the browser. The ERP workers already keep their views this way; the mail and tender workers do not share theirs.
2. **Share what was learned about a site between workers.** Today each of the nine mail searches rediscovers on its own which query returns nothing and which returns the three result pages. A shared note of "searches tried on this site and their hit counts" would cut steps, and mail is the largest token consumer (about a third).
3. **Let one model-chosen step read more.** `open_pages` already does this for the ERP (up to ten link targets the model picked, in one call). The same pattern could cover the mail result list: the model picks the search, a helper pages through and opens the hits.

I'd put item 2 first: it is the only one that reduces both tokens and time, and it is clearly model-directed. It is a real change to the mail module, so it needs its own test runs.

again isnt that overfitting? yes or no

No.

None of the three ideas encodes anything about the public sites: no URLs, labels, page structure or values. They store and share whatever the model itself chose to open or search at run time, so on a private site with a different layout they simply hold different content.

They would become overfitting only if implemented with public-site assumptions baked in, for example a helper that knows the mailbox has two folders or that results come in three pages. The rule to hold to is that the model picks the search and the pages, and the helper only remembers and repeats what the model picked.

class OldLongResultsLeaveTheHistory(unittest.TestCase):
    def history(self):
        from pydantic_ai.messages import ModelRequest, ToolReturnPart, UserPromptPart
        view = "URL: https://erp.test/m/1\nTitle: Material\n\n" + "record line\n" * 50
        batch = lambda n: "\n\n".join(f"=== /view/{n}{k}\n" + "value line\n" * 120 for k in "ab") + \
            f"\n\nLinks on these views you have not opened yet: /view/{n}c"
        return [ModelRequest(parts=[UserPromptPart(content="Goal\n\nCurrent view:\n" + view)]),
                ModelRequest(parts=[ToolReturnPart(tool_name="open_pages", content=batch(1), tool_call_id="1")]),
                ModelRequest(parts=[ToolReturnPart(tool_name="open_pages", content=batch(2), tool_call_id="2")]),
                ModelRequest(parts=[ToolReturnPart(tool_name="open_pages", content="already opened", tool_call_id="3")])]

    def test_only_the_newest_long_result_stays_whole(self):
        import worker
        out = worker._forget_old_views(self.history())
        first, second, third = (m.parts[0].content for m in out[1:])
        self.assertLess(len(first), 300)
        self.assertIn("=== /view/1a", first)
        self.assertIn("=== /view/1b", first)
        self.assertIn("/view/1c", first)  # what it said was still to open
        self.assertIn("value line", second)  # the newest batch is whole
        self.assertEqual(third, "already opened")

    def test_a_single_long_result_is_left_alone(self):
        import worker
        history = self.history()[:2]
        self.assertEqual(worker._forget_old_views(history)[1].parts[0].content, history[1].parts[0].content)
