Update while the rerun on the starter eval is going:

## Scouting-site run with the new mail search

It reached the review page with the same correct five positions and matching totals, in 162 s. The new search worked, but it was not faster in this run:

- **Clef marking:** right every time it had real hits (0.84–0.96 for the record, 0.02–0.05 for other rows), and 6 messages were opened straight from its marks.
- **Mail kinds still took 18–74 s.** A search in a folder with no hits returns a few unrelated rows, so the worker still spends steps going folder by folder and rewording.
- **Approval:** Clef marked only one of the versions, so the worker kept the rest itself.

So this is working plumbing with no measured time gain yet. The saving would have to come from fewer folder-by-folder steps, which this tool does not remove.

## What the starter eval found

On its very first try on a world it had never seen, our agent would have scored close to zero, from two small things:

- **No scenario date in the brief:** our research raised an error 2.3 s in and ended with no positions at all. A brief without a date now means today, with a note on the board.
- **Tender reference read with its title attached** (`VG-2026-0142, "Hydraulikzylinder …"`), which makes a bid ineligible. The brief reader is now told to take the identifier alone.

That is the "small things causing leveraged impact" the sponsor message describes, and neither shows up on public-1. Separately, with no answer to enter, the bid form worker paged back and forth until its step limit, the same loop the first local run showed.

I'll report the eval rerun's score when it ends. Nothing is committed.

Not in a way that would help us: it is the same Qwen3.8-Flash-Next we already use, only compressed, and the rules don't let us run it ourselves.

- **Not smarter.** It is NVIDIA's 4-bit quantized copy of the same model. On its own benchmark table it is within about a point of the 8-bit version (for example 91.5 against 92.0, 82.9 against 83.3), with a few tests slightly up and a few slightly down. That is noise, not a better model.
- **Faster only for whoever hosts it.** Quantization makes the checkpoint about 2.7× smaller, so it serves faster on NVIDIA Blackwell B200/B300 GPUs. That is a gain for the server, not something we can switch on from the agent.
- **We can't run it.** The fair-play page lists "bundling or running a local model, or reaching any model other than through the proxy" as a violation, and the 20 MB package limit rules it out anyway.
- **The only legal route** is an allowed provider that serves it (OpenRouter, Together, Fireworks and so on) with our own key through the platform's proxy. That would be metered at the provider's price instead of the hosted model's simulated price, and I haven't checked whether any of them offers this exact build.

The platform doesn't say which build its hosted Qwen is. The sponsor message that decode got 2–3× quicker would fit a change like this one, but that is my guess.

The local run on the starter eval finished: the brief fixes worked, but the agent ended with no positions and never submitted, so it would score 0 there. The sandbox run on the deployed copy is still in flight (in the bid form at about 310 s).

## What happened locally on the starter world

- **Now right:** tender reference (`VG-2026-0142`), the missing scenario date (today was used), and the discount (3.5%, read from the mailbox in 15 s).
- **No requirement was read.** The starter specification states bore, stroke, mounting and certification, but no operating pressure and no catalogue group. Our requirement record demands both, so all three requirements were thrown away and every position was omitted.
- **No bid was submitted.** With nothing to enter, the form worker used up its steps three times (45, 30, 15) and the run ended without an answer. Even an empty bid would have earned the reference and discount points.
- **Other signs:** two specification attempts were stopped by the loop guard, and the Q&A worker ran out of its 28 steps on a portal that has no Q&A.

## What this means

The starter world is not a re-skin of the real task; it has six simpler rules instead of 29, so part of this failure is "different task", not "different website". The private set uses the real rules, where pressure and catalogue group are stated by rule. Two things carry over regardless:

1. **One missing value should not drop a whole requirement.** Today any unreadable attribute discards the requirement and with it the position.
2. **The run must always end with a submitted bid**, even an empty one. Ending with no answer is the worst outcome and it happened here.

## Decision for you

How far to generalise beyond the 29 rules:

- **Narrow (my recommendation):** fix the two points above, and spend the eval effort on worlds that follow the real rules with different sites and data, built from our `dev/synth` scenarios. That tests what the private set actually varies.
- **Broad:** also make the agent cope with the starter's simplified task (no pressure, no catalogue group, ERP search by attributes). It would pass the starter eval, but it changes the core matching logic for a case the final probably doesn't contain.

I'll report the sandbox eval run when it ends.

    """
    Hooks for the other workers' facts: scoped amendments from the tender Q&A (already filtered to the right sender
    by the caller; revision and requirement scoping and latest-wins happen here) and the per-end reserve values of
    the revision-specific Technikfreigabe, by reserve key. Without a needed reserve the stroke stays open.
    """
    base: dict[str, Decimal | str] = {"bore": req.bore, "stroke": req.stroke, "pressure": req.pressure,

    pending: list[str] = []
    stroke: Decimal | None = Decimal(str(attrs["stroke"]))
    if req.stroke_is_usable:
        reserve = (reserves or {}).get(req.reserve_key or "")

Both fixes are in and the full unit suite passes (329 tests); a local rerun on the starter eval is going to check them.

## The screenshots

They are frames from the sponsors' 34-second demo of the new Evals feature, the same thing we just used:

1. **Create (CLI + MCP):** a coding agent is asked to "make an eval from the starter kit" and calls `eval_init`, which writes the starter world (tender portal, mailbox, ERP, supplier catalogue) with its `expected.json`.
2. **Deploy:** `atira eval deploy ./my-eval` creates a private eval, uploads about 15 files and builds it in seconds. This is the step we ran for `ev_b72e6601bff81dc1`.
3. **Run:** `atira eval run my-eval --package ...` runs different packages on the same world: the latest submission, the latest test run, or a folder. The demo switches git branches and runs each one, the last with `--repeats 3`.
4. **Leaderboard:** each eval version gets a table of entries by quality and time. In the demo the two feature branches score 100 and 92.5, ahead of the submission (81.4) and the test package (64).

The point of the demo is the workflow in frames 3 and 4: run several of your own branches on a world that isn't public-1 and compare them side by side before choosing what to submit.

## The two fixes

- **A missing value no longer drops a requirement.** If the specification states no bore or no pressure, that attribute is simply not compared; the requirement and its position stay. A value that is present but unreadable still counts as a reading error, as before. A requirement with no catalogue group is kept but not searched in the ERP, and is not sent back for retries.
- **Last resort for forms with no way to omit a position.** The form instructions and the final "submit now" pass tell the worker what to do on such a form: enter only the minimum the form requires and go on, because a bid that is never submitted scores nothing.

One thing to be aware of on the second fix: on such a form the minimum entries are placeholders (first offered option, a zero price), not researched values. It only applies when the form has no omit option, which public-1 does have, so the normal flow is unchanged.

On the starter world the first fix alone will not produce positions, because that world names no catalogue group and we agreed not to add ERP search by attributes. What I expect from the rerun is a submitted bid with the reference and discount right, instead of no answer.

The local rerun on the starter world finished while the sandbox run is still in flight: the first fix worked, the second got further but still did not submit, and I've added one more change for that.

- **Requirements kept:** all three were read (`A-10`, `A-20`, `A-30`) with no pressure stated. As expected, none was searched in the ERP because the world names no catalogue group, so the answer still had no positions.
- **Form got through but ran out of passes:** with the new last-resort instruction the worker did get past all three position pages and reached "Prüfen und signieren" (step 8 of 8). It arrived there on its final 15-step pass with 708 s still left, and the run ended without requesting the TAN.
- **Added fix:** the final "submit what is on screen" pass now repeats (up to four times, 15 steps each) while the bid is not in and time remains. It stops at once if a pass errors, which is what happens when the platform closes the model token after an accepted bid.

Two caveats on that local run:

- The review page showed a 0% discount and zero prices: the worker entered placeholders and never entered the 3.5% discount it had read, so a bid submitted from that state would not have earned the discount points.
- The local eval server had been up for about 40 minutes and was refusing some logins by then, so that run is not a clean test.

The sandbox run now in flight was packaged before the repeat-pass change, so it may well end the same way (on the signing page, no answer). I'll report it when it ends; if it does end that way, one more run with the current package is the real test of the second fix.

The second sandbox run on the deployed starter eval submitted a bid and scored 20 (`run_2aba3206e2cd6e15`, 4:06, $0.043), up from 0 with no answer.

| | First run | Second run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Submitted | no | yes |
| Quality | 0 | 20 |
| Tender reference | not scored | 5 of 5 |
| Discount | not scored | 5 of 5 |
| Positions | not scored | 10 of 75 (two positions earned 5 each, the third 0) |
| Net total | not scored | 0 of 15 |

What happened in it:

- **Requirements:** all three were read this time, with no pressure stated. None was searched in the ERP, because the world names no catalogue group.
- **Form:** the worker used the last-resort instruction, got through the position pages in 40 steps, reached signing, fetched the TAN and submitted. The discount of 3.5% was entered correctly.
- **Position points:** these came from placeholder entries, not research. The two positions that scored 5 did so on parts such as quantity or lead time matching by the way they were filled in.

So both fixes did what they were meant to: a missing attribute no longer drops the requirement, and the run ends with a submitted bid. The remaining 80 points on this world are the positions, which need an ERP search without a catalogue group. That is the "broad" option we set aside because the real rules always name one.

This run did not include the repeat-pass change I made afterwards; it wasn't needed here since the first signing pass succeeded. Nothing is committed yet.

The platform sets no API key variables of its own, except the run-token placeholder for a provider the
organizers pay for (above). `setup` runs first, with network (install your dependencies there) but without the
run's variables or your team secrets, and nothing it starts survives into the run. The run itself reaches only our API and the challenge's websites,
through that proxy; Chromium is already configured to use it. A scored run of RFQ has 20 minutes; a run that
ends without an answer scores 0.

## Browsers

The sandbox starts one browser unless `agent.json` asks for more, up to four:

```json
{"setup": ["uv", "sync"], "run": ["uv", "run", "python", "agent.py"], "browsers": 3}
```

`browsers` is a whole number from 1 to 4; anything else rejects the package with
`Invalid agent.json: browsers: must be a whole number from 1 to 4`. Browser n is its own headful Chromium with its
own profile, on display `:n` (1280×800) with the Chrome DevTools Protocol on port 9221 + n (9222 to 9225), behind
the same proxy as browser 1. All of them are ready before the clock starts. `CDP_URL` stays browser 1, `CDP_URLS` lists all of
them in order, and `BROWSER_COUNT` says how many there are. With three:

websites and hands everything to the model at the end.

## The browser

In the sandbox a headful Chromium runs on the desktop (`DISPLAY=:1`, 1280×800) with CDP on
`127.0.0.1:9222`.

- **DOM agents:** attach with Playwright (`chromium.connect_over_cdp(CDP_URL)`) or any CDP client.
- **Pixel agents:** take screenshots and send mouse and keyboard input to the desktop (`xdotool` and
  ImageMagick's `import` are installed), for example to drive Claude's computer-use tool.
- **Locally:** without `CDP_URL`, launch your own Chromium. The websites are the same: `eval "$(atira scout --env)"`

content.text:
Yes. Reading the sites does not need Playwright or any browser, and I just confirmed it on the public sites with a plain Python HTTP client: sign-in worked on three of the four in about a second each, with no browser involved.

## What the test showed

| Site | Plain HTTP sign-in |
| --- | --- |
| Tender portal | accepted in 0.9 s, lands on the cookie-consent page |
| Customer portal | accepted in 0.8 s, same |
| ERP | accepted in 1.2 s, same |
| Mail | timed out at 20 s on this try |

The sign-in is an ordinary form (a hidden token plus username and password), so a generic "fill whatever login form the page has" works. The consent page that follows is one more form to post; I stopped there. I did not test past it, so whether the "not a robot" slider or the ERP notice gate are enforced by the server is still open.

## Why this works in the sandbox

The run contract says the sandbox's only way out is an HTTP proxy that reaches the platform and the websites. Any HTTP client that uses that proxy can talk to the sites directly. Our own code comment saying the sites resolve "only in the browser" is true only for a client that ignores the proxy.

## Is it allowed?

- **Allowed:** the rule is "don't start browsers of your own", and an HTTP client is not a browser. The docs also say "Playwright or any CDP client", so Playwright itself is never required.
- **Still required:** a model must choose what to open and search. An HTTP crawler that grabs everything first is rejected exactly like a browser crawler.

## Is the top team doing this?

I can't see their code, so I don't know. Their numbers (38 s, $0.026) fit it: no page rendering, no waiting for pages to settle, fetches in parallel, and few model calls. Skipping the browser alone would not get us there, though. Our time is mostly about 280 model steps at 2–3 s each; page loads are only 0.6–1.1 s of each step.

## What I'd do with it

A hybrid, not a rewrite:

1. **Keep the browser for sign-in, gates and the bid form.** Those are the parts built for clicking, and the part most likely to differ on the private sites.
2. **Read model-chosen pages over HTTP with the browser's session cookies, in parallel.** A material's ten views are opened one after another today (about 6 s); fetched together they would take about 1 s. If a fetch comes back as a sign-in or gate page, fall back to the browser for that page.
3. **Then cut model steps**, which is where most of the time is.

The risk is generalisation: tooltips and hidden text come through fine in raw HTML, but content that a page builds with JavaScript would be missing, which is why the browser fallback matters.

## Testing without Playwright

- **Whole agent:** not today, since every worker drives a tab. It would become possible for the reading parts after step 2.
- **Model only:** yes, already. The readers take saved page text and need no browser; `dev/clef_eval` and the `dev/research_check*.py` scripts work that way.
- **Sites:** `atira eval dev` serves a world on localhost that plain HTTP can reach.

Say if you want me to build step 2; I'd start with the ERP material views, where the gain is easiest to measure.
for now, cContinue with the current approach. No need to change stuff. Go against the public evals and iterate over what can be improved.

# Prepare a tender response

You work in sales engineering for Beispiel Hydraulik GmbH, a German hydraulics manufacturer. Prepare one net EUR bid for Wasserverband Musterstadt: Hydraulikzylinder für das Schleusentor Süd (VG-2026-0815). The scenario date is 2026-10-08T09:00:00Z; the tender deadline is 2026-10-30T11:00:00Z.

Collect the tender and its clarifications from the tender portal (Vergabeportal, `tender-portal`), the technical specification from the buyer's supplier portal (Lieferantenportal, `customer-portal`), materials and prices from the internal ERP (`erp`), and discount approvals from the sales mailbox in the webmail (Werkpost, `mail`

## Rules

1. Quantity: start with the original tender quantity. For each position, use the quantity in the latest dated clarification that changes that position, if any.
2. Requirement: use the requirement referenced by the position in the specification revision marked current. Superseded revisions do not apply.
3. Material: select an active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification all exactly equal that requirement. Blocked materials do not qualify. If any position has no matching active material, submit no_bid.
4. Unit price: use the material's price condition valid on the scenario date, including both validity endpoints. Choose the scale with the highest minimum quantity no greater than the final quantity. Apply the approved discount to that scale price and round the resulting unit price half up to the nearest cent.
5. Discount: use the most recent message from the sales director (leitung@ followed by the bidder's mailbox domain) that approves a discount for this exact tender reference. Approvals for other references and messages from other senders do not apply. If there is no approval, use zero percent.
6. Lead time: use the delivery-from-stock lead time in weeks when stock covers the final quantity; otherwise use the production lead time in weeks.
7. Total: sum each final quantity multiplied by its rounded discounted unit price, then round the total net amount half up to the nearest cent.
8. Decision: submit bid with one entry per tender position, identified by its position number, and currency EUR. If any active matching material is missing, submit no_bid with no positions and a total of zero.


## Additional rules

These refine rules 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 above. Every submitted quantity is in pieces.

- Partial submission: full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving
- Finding records: the specification/data sheet names a Kataloggruppe for each requirement. Search the ERP for that group, then compare candidate attributes. Empty or over-broad searches do not list the catalogue; narrow to at most 20 results. Mail search combines words with AND: use the tender reference plus a subject/topic. Re
- Agent requirement: a language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. They must not autono
- Commercial clauses: a tender Q&A answer may assign a position to a Konditionsgruppe. Resolve that key in the latest Konditionsregeln message for the exact reference from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. Its prose determines whether discount applies to base only, base plus mass surcharge, or neither; setup fees are 
- Withdrawn answers: a tender Q&A answer may withdraw (zurückziehen) an earlier answer by its number. Ignore the withdrawn answer's quantity change; the latest remaining change applies, otherwise the tender quantity.
- Scoped amendments: after selecting the governing full specification revision, read the tender Q&A for technical amendments naming that revision and requirement. Apply only the named attributes; all others are inherited. The latest dated applicable amendment wins per attribute. Amendments to other revisions do not apply.
- Shared stock: sum final quantities of all positions selecting the same material. Stock must cover that entire sum for every such position to use stock delivery; otherwise all use production delivery. No partial stock allocation. Price scales remain per position, not per material sum.
- Conditional discount: the latest exact-reference director approval may require a minimum undiscounted net order value. Compute that value from final quantities and valid per-position scale prices before any discount and excluding mass surcharges and setup fees, rounded half up to cents. The threshold is inclusive. If it fails,
- Units: tender and Q&A quantities use the position's stated unit. Convert Satz using the governing specification's pieces per set. Price scales, inventory, allocation weights and bid quantities all use final pieces. Carton rounding affects packaging cost only, never the bid quantity.
- Pricing breakdown: base_unit_price, surcharge_per_unit, packaging_per_unit and rebate_total are optional and earn independent credit. All monetary answers are net EUR. Base, surcharge and packaging are per piece; rebate_total is the credit for the whole position. Enter 0.00 for a known zero; blank means unanswered. Do not feed
- These calculation rules apply to both practice and private datasets. Missing calculation fields lose only their own points; signing an incomplete bid is supported.
- Technical derivation: for a requirement marked nutzbarer Weg, apply its scoped amendments first, then add twice the per-end reserve from the revision-specific Technikfreigabe. Match the resulting nominal stroke to the ERP. Do not change the other attributes.
- Authority and time: resolve each key from the latest record no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender reference. Authorized subjects/senders (local part + bidder mailbox domain): Technikfreigabe/technik, Verpackungstarife/logistik, Terminfreigabe/logistik, Devisenfixing/finanzen, Rüstpools/kalkulation, Projektbonus

The package is the `agent/` folder minus what `.gitignore` excludes: 55 files, about 289 KB compressed. The platform would not hand back the archive for an eval run, so the list below is from `atira test-run ./agent --dry-run`, which shows exactly what would upload right now, and I built a local copy with the same files.

**How it runs** (`agent.json`): setup `uv sync`, run `uv run --no-sync python agent.py`, models `qwen` and `clef`, 4 browsers.

**Every file in it:**

| Group | Files |
| --- | --- |
| Entry and contract | `agent.json` (136 B), `agent.py` (8.8 KB), `run.py` (4.2 KB), `browsers.py` (3.3 KB), `localenv.py` (1.9 KB), `models.py` (2.1 KB) |
| Orchestration | `orchestrator.py` (78.4 KB), `board.py` (6.2 KB), `verify.py` (8.5 KB), `briefing.py` (3.2 KB) |
| Research | `research.py` (78.8 KB), `research_mail.py` (51.8 KB), `research_tender.py` (33.8 KB), `site_tools.py` (33.0 KB), `evidence.py` (25.5 KB) |
| Browser and worker | `browser_tools.py` (48.5 KB), `extract.py` (14.0 KB), `worker.py` (11.9 KB), `vision.py` (3.0 KB), `loopwatch.py` (3.1 KB) |
| Models | `llm.py` (31.1 KB), `clef.py` (7.0 KB) |
| Calculation and bid form | `calc.py` (30.2 KB), `submit.py` (56.4 KB), `configurator.py` (17.3 KB) |
| Logging | `tracing.py` (2.4 KB) |
| Project files | `pyproject.toml` (432 B), `uv.lock` (185.4 KB), `README.md` (5.2 KB), `.gitignore` (69 B), `.env.example` (794 B) |
| Tests (24 files, about 238 KB) | `tests/test_bid_flow.py`, `test_calc.py`, `test_complete.py`, `test_configurator.py`, `test_decision_robustness.py`, `test_evidence.py`, `test_extract.py`, `test_fast_start.py`, `test_fit.py`, `test_hang.py`, `test_kit.py`, `test_llm.py`, `test_llm_anthropic.py`, `test_llm_watchdog.py`, `test_localenv.py`, `test_orchestrator.py`, `test_parallel.py`, `test_research_mail.py`, `test_reselect.py`, `test_revision.py`, `test_revive.py`, `test_site_tools.py`, `test_slow_start.py`, `test_v3.py` |

**Left out by `.gitignore`:** `.venv`, `traces`, `__pycache__`, `tests/__pycache__`, `.ruff_cache`.

Two things worth knowing:

- This is the working tree, so it includes today's uncommitted changes. A submission should be packed from committed code (`git archive HEAD agent`), as the project notes say, so that nothing unreviewed goes to the package reviewer.
- The tests ride along in every upload. They are harmless, but they are about 80% of the source by size after `uv.lock`; leaving them out would shrink what the reviewer has to read.

To list or unpack the local copy yourself: `tar -tzvf <path>` or `tar -xzf <path> -C <folder>`.

def resolve_mail(results: list[KindResult], reference: str, domain: str, scenario: datetime, mailbox: str
                 ) -> MailFacts:
    facts = MailFacts(mailbox=mailbox)
    scenario = _aware(scenario)
    if not domain:  # never drop what was read for a missing address: the messages name their recipient
        domain = bidder_domain(mailbox, [r for res in results for r in res.records])
        facts.problems.append(f"mailbox address not shown; bidder domain from the recipients: {domain or 'none'}")
    for res in results:
        kind = res.kind
        facts.seconds[kind.name] = res.seconds
        valid = valid_records(res.records, reference, kind, domain, scenario)
        try:
            used = _apply(facts, kind, valid)
        except ParseError as error:
            facts.problems.append(f"{kind.name}: {error}")
            used = set()
        for rec in res.records:
            facts.sources.append(Source(kind=kind.name, subject=rec.subject, sender=rec.sender, sent_at=rec.sent_at,
                                        reference=rec.reference, is_record=rec.is_record,
                                        has_content=rec.content is not None, used=id(rec) in used))
    return facts

The local run on the synth platform-hazards world gave a full trace, and it shows exactly where the points went. That run (before today's last fixes) submitted a bid in 787 s and scored 36.9; here is each loss and what I changed.

| Lost | Cause found in the trace | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Discount, 0 of 5 | The approval was read correctly (5%). It was then discarded because the brief names the director as "Name <address>" and our sender check compared that whole string to the address. | When the brief gives an address, the address decides. Messages that are read and all set aside are now reported. |
| Quantities on two positions | The Q&A page was collected in full (it shows 146→158 and 360→372). The reader then failed with "token limit exceeded before any response" (it used its whole output budget thinking), and the failure was silent. | Thinking calls get an explicit output limit of 16,000 tokens; a failed reading is retried once without thinking; an unread Q&A is reported as a problem. |
| Material numbers on two positions | The research chose all four materials correctly. The form on this world asks for a catalogue group first, which our form helper had no value for, so it refused each position and the model then typed wrong numbers by hand. | The catalogue group is now one of the values the form helper can enter, and its message for a mismatched control says to remap it. |
| Unit prices and total | Follow from the discount and quantities above. | — |
| Time (787 s) | Seven mail searches for record kinds that don't exist on this world ran 150–180 s each, twice. | Mail searches now stop once nothing refers to their kind. |

Two more fixes from the other evals went in with these:

- A material status written as a plain word no longer counts as unread; that is why the no-bid eval scored 0.
- A material worker that used all its steps is not sent over the same record again.

The tests for every changed module pass (149). I have not rerun the whole suite since you stopped it earlier.

- **Sandbox** `run_6098e12b4289349c` on this eval. It has the mail-by-demand change but not the sender, Q&A or catalogue-group fixes, which I made after it started.
- **Local** run on the same world with everything, for a scored result and a full trace.

python3 - <<'EOF'
p='agent/research_mail.py'; s=open(p).read()
anchor='''def kind_budget(now: float, deadline: float | None) -> float:'''
assert s.count(anchor)==1
new='''# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the survey: one look at the mailbox for all kinds
#
# A mailbox is read like a person reads it: list what there is for this tender, once per folder, see from the
# subjects which message is which record, and open those. Searching once per record kind instead meant nine workers
# typing into the same search box of the same mailbox, each finding out the same things again, and going on to
# search for records that were plainly not in a list they had in front of them (seen: seven searches of 150 s each,
# twice, in a mailbox of fourteen messages). Here a model lists the tender's messages (it chooses the folders and
# the search), a model says which row is which record, and the chosen messages are opened and read side by side.
# A record kind the survey found nothing for is searched on its own afterwards, by the worker below, only if
# something refers to it.

SURVEY_SECONDS = 120.0  # listing the folders, at most; it takes five to eight steps
SURVEY_STEPS = 14
SURVEY_ROWS = 200  # rows the survey keeps
SURVEY_OPEN = 8  # messages opened at one time


@dataclass
class SurveyRow:
    text: str
    url: str  # the address the row opens, '' for a row that is not a link
    where: str  # the list it was seen in (its page address)


SURVEY_GOAL = """\\
List this mailbox's messages for tender {reference}, in every folder the mailbox has (for example inbox and
archive). In each folder call list_messages: with the mailbox's search field and the reference {reference} as the
query (a search combines words with AND, so the reference alone finds every message about this tender), or with no
arguments to take the list the folder shows as it is, when that folder has no search or shows only a few messages.
It pages through the whole list and remembers every row. Do not open messages and do not search for single
topics: the rows are sorted into records afterwards. As soon as every folder is listed, return a one-line
summary."""


def list_tool(index: list[SurveyRow]):
    """A tool that takes the message list the model chose (a search of its choosing, or the folder as shown) to
    its last page and remembers the rows."""

    async def list_messages(ctx: RunContext[Deps], field_ref: str = "", query: str = "", submit_ref: str = "") -> str:
        """List messages and remember every row: with `field_ref` and `query`, type the query into that search
        field and submit it (Enter, or click `submit_ref`) first; with no arguments, take the list the page shows
        now. The list is paged to its end. You choose the folder (open it first), the field and the words."""
        session: SiteSession = ctx.deps.session
        if field_ref.strip() and query.strip():
            listing, header = await site_tools.search_rows(session, field_ref, query, submit_ref or None)
            if listing is None:
                return header
        else:
            listing = await site_tools.paginate(session)
            header = f"{len(listing.rows)} rows ({listing.how}). URL: {session.page.url}"
        host = urlparse(session.site["url"]).netloc
        known = {row.url for row in index if row.url}
        added = 0
        for row in listing.rows:
            url = row_link(row, session.page.url, host) or ""
            if (url and url in known) or len(index) >= SURVEY_ROWS:
                continue
            if not url and any(r.text == row.text and not r.url for r in index):
                continue
            index.append(SurveyRow(text=row.text[:400], url=url, where=session.page.url))
            known.add(url)
            added += 1
        session.trace.event(session.name, "list_messages", query=query, rows=len(listing.rows), pages=listing.pages,
                            added=added, total=len(index))
        shown = "\\n".join(f"- {row.text[:160]}" for row in listing.rows[:6])
        return (f"{header}\\nRemembered {added} new row(s), {len(index)} in all so far."
                + (f" The first rows:\\n{shown}" if shown else " This list is empty.")
                + "\\nIf another folder is not listed yet, open it and list it; otherwise return.")

    return list_messages


class Assigned(BaseModel):
    kind: str = Field(description="The record kind's name, exactly as given")
    rows: list[int] = Field(description="Numbers of the rows that are this record; [] if none is")


class Assignment(BaseModel):
    kinds: list[Assigned]


ASSIGN_INSTRUCTIONS = """\\
You get the message list of a company mailbox for one tender (each row with its number and what the list shows:
sender, subject, date) and the record kinds that are looked for. For each kind, name the rows that are that record
for exactly the tender reference given.
- The reference must be exactly this one: with any extra prefix, suffix or digit it is another tender.
- A record's subject names its topic. Older and newer versions of a record share a subject: name all of them.
- A request for a record, a reply, a notice, a newsletter or a message on another topic is not the record.
- A row belongs to one kind at most. When you cannot tell from the row whether it is the record, include it: it
  is opened and checked afterwards.
Use only row numbers from the list, and only the kind names given."""


async def assign_rows(rows: list[SurveyRow], kinds: list[Kind], reference: str) -> dict[str, list[SurveyRow]]:
    """Which rows are which record kind, by one model call over the whole list."""
    if not rows or not kinds:
        return {}
    names = {kind.name for kind in kinds}
    agent = Agent(reader_model(), output_type=Assignment, instructions=ASSIGN_INSTRUCTIONS,
                  model_settings=llm.settings(thinking=False, timeout=READ_TIMEOUT), retries=3)

    @agent.output_validator
    def _known(out: Assignment) -> Assignment:
        wrong = sorted({a.kind for a in out.kinds} - names)
        beyond = sorted({n for a in out.kinds for n in a.rows if not 1 <= n <= len(rows)})
        if wrong or beyond:
            raise ModelRetry(f"Unknown kind names {wrong} or row numbers {beyond}: use only the kinds "
                             f"{sorted(names)} and rows 1 to {len(rows)}.")
        return out

    listing = "\\n".join(f"{i}. {row.text}" for i, row in enumerate(rows, 1))
    wanted = "\\n".join(f"- {kind.name}: {kind.what} (subject or topic {kind.subject!r}, sender {kind.sender!r})"
                       for kind in kinds)
    out = (await agent.run(f"Tender reference: {reference}\\n\\nRecord kinds:\\n{wanted}\\n\\nRows:\\n{listing}")).output
    assigned: dict[str, list[SurveyRow]] = {}
    for a in out.kinds:
        for n in dict.fromkeys(a.rows):
            assigned.setdefault(a.kind, []).append(rows[n - 1])
    return assigned


async def survey(session: SiteSession, kinds: list[Kind], reference: str, deadline: float | None = None
                 ) -> dict[str, KindResult]:

content.text:
To your question about the tabs: every worker gets its own tab so that independent work runs side by side. It helps when the pages really are different (ten ERP materials read at once instead of one after another), and it does not help when the workers all do the same thing in the same place, which is exactly what the mailbox was: nine tabs, nine sign-ins, nine workers typing into the same search box. Each extra tab is also another sign-in and more page loads on a site that slows down under load; in one run today five of the nine mail tabs failed to open.

## The mail rewrite

The mailbox is now read the way a person reads it:

1. **List once.** One worker opens each folder and lists the tender's messages (it chooses the folders and the search; a helper pages the list to its end).
2. **Sort the rows.** One model call says which row is which record, for all record kinds at once.
3. **Read side by side.** The chosen messages are opened and read in parallel, in short-lived tabs that close again.
4. **Search only what's missing and needed.** A record kind the survey found nothing for is searched on its own only if something in the tender, specification or ERP refers to it.

Mail tabs go from nine to four (one surveys, the rest are for step 4). The reference, sender and date rules that decide which record counts are unchanged. If the survey fails for any reason, the old per-kind search runs as before.

## Also fixed just now

The discount on the synth world was still 0 after my first sender fix. The new "messages read, none counts" report showed why: the reader had copied the sender as "Name <address>", so the comparison failed from the other side. The address is now extracted on both sides.

## Where things stand

- **Local run before the rewrite** (all other fixes): 57.5 on the synth world, up from 36.9. Materials, quantities and lead times were right; everything still lost traced to the discount.
- **Local run with the rewrite and the sender fix:** just started.
- **Sandbox runs** `run_3ac455cd456226f4` and `run_6098e12b4289349c`: still running, both from before the rewrite.

The tests for the changed modules pass. After the local run I'll check the rewrite against the public scouting mailbox too, since that one has several result pages and the human-check widgets, before any sandbox run with it.

content.text:
Yes, the older package scored higher on that eval (66.3 against 57.5), but the breakdowns show it is not because the older code is better. Each run lost points on one different thing, and the newer run's loss is the sender bug I finished fixing after it had started.

**How the eval score is built (out of 100):** tender reference 5, discount 5, net total 15, and 75 for the positions shared equally. This world has four positions, so 18.75 each, split into material, quantity, unit price and lead time.

| | Older package (`run_6098…`, mail-by-demand only) | Newer package (`run_3ac4…`, "all fixes") |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quality | 66.3 | 57.5 |
| Time | 13:39 | 11:36 |
| Reference | 5 of 5 | 5 of 5 |
| Discount | 5 of 5 (read as 5%) | 0 of 5 (entered as 0%) |
| Positions entered | 3 of 4, each fully right; position 01.04 missing | all 4, with material, quantity and lead time right on every one |
| Unit prices | right on the 3 entered | wrong on all 4, only because the discount was 0 |
| Net total | 0 of 15 (a position missing) | 0 of 15 (follows from the discount) |

What that means:

- **The newer run got more of the hard part right.** All four materials, both changed quantities from the Q&A and all lead times are correct. Those are what the Q&A and catalogue-group fixes were for.
- **Its whole loss is the discount.** In that run the reader wrote the sender as "Name <address>", and my first sender fix only handled that spelling on the brief's side. I fixed the other side about twenty minutes ago; that fix is not in either sandbox run. With the discount at 5%, every unit price and the total in that run would match, which is 100.
- **The older run got the discount by luck of spelling.** There the reader happened to write the bare address, so the old comparison passed. It then lost a whole position.

So the comparison is two runs that each tripped on one thing, not a regression. The package that has both the complete sender fix and the mail rewrite has only run locally so far, and that run is still going; it is the one to judge.

- **The rewrite itself worked:** one worker listed both folders (7 rows), one call picked out the two approval messages, and both were read by 48 s into the run. Before, the approval alone took 55–70 s and seven other searches ran alongside it.
- **Survey re-listing the same folder:** the survey worker kept calling the list tool on a folder it had already listed, until its 14 steps ran out (34 s where about 10 would do). The tool now says a list was already taken, and a third listing of the same list ends the survey.
- **Searches for records nobody has asked for yet:** two single searches (exchange rates and stroke reserves) still ran about 130 s while waiting for the ERP to say whether they were needed. After a completed survey, a single search now waits until something actually refers to that record, and only for as long as that source is still being read.

The tests for the changed modules pass (41). The sandbox run includes both adjustments; the local run that prompted them does not, so its timing will look worse than this run's should.

I'll report the score when it ends.

The sandbox run with the mail rewrite scored 100 on the synth platform-hazards eval (`run_16684b875d29c106`): reference, discount and total right, and all four positions at full points. It took 10:30 and cost $0.19.

| Run on this eval | Quality | Time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Our ranked submission (a teammate's run) | 10 | 11:39 |
| This branch, first try | cut off before submitting | — |
| Mail-by-demand only | 66.3 | 13:39 |
| First sender fix, Q&A and catalogue-group fixes | 57.5 | 11:36 |
| Mail rewrite and complete sender fix | 100 | 10:30 |

**Where the 10:30 went.** Mail was done by 47 s. The rest was the ERP: three of the four catalogue-group searches returned no list at first and only succeeded when the coverage check sent them back, the last one at about 490 s.

**Why those searches failed.** The local trace shows that world's ERP search form is a dead end by design: it always answers "please give a catalogue group; the value help lists the groups", whatever is typed. The worker had the value help open, with a link for exactly its group, then went back to the form and tried it eight times.

**Fix just made (not in that run):** the search worker is told not to resend a refused search and to take the route the page itself names, and its loop warning is switched on so that the same refusal three times gets it told to use a control it hasn't used. The tests for the changed modules pass.

The sandbox test run on the public data with the mail rewrite has just started its agent; I'll report it when it ends. That run does not include the ERP search fix above, which I made after it was packaged.

- Each message is opened once and gets 75 s at most; a page that hangs is dropped and its record kind is searched on its own.
- The survey worker gets 24 steps instead of 14.
- A survey that ran out of steps or time is marked incomplete, so nothing is concluded from a record being absent and the missing kinds are searched straight away.

content.text:
Strategies first, as you asked. They are based on the leaderboard and on a step-by-step timing of our last full run on the public data.

## Where we stand

| Team | Quality | Cost | Time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Plite | 100 | $0.026 | 0:38 |
| PolyETHylen | 100 | $0.024 | 1:38 |
| BaoByte | 100 | $0.033 | 1:56 |
| error404.ai (#7) | 100 | $0.110 | 7:33 |

The leaders spend about a quarter of our tokens. At 38 s a run can only have 15 to 20 model calls in a row, so Plite is almost certainly not rendering a page in a browser for every step.

## Where our time goes

This is the 336 s local run, which stops just before signing:

| Stage | Seconds | What held it up |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start, brief, plan | 8 | fine |
| Specification | 113 | had the revision list at 55 s, then wandered until the loop guard ended it at 75 s; two page reads took 22 s and 28 s |
| ERP search | 25 | waits for the specification |
| Material reads | 20 typical | two outliers at 50 s and 80 s kept the stage open until 221 s |
| Mail | finished at 284 s | one record kind was missed by the survey, waited for the ERP, then took 62 s on its own |
| Bid form | 43 | six positions one after another, then a final pass of 6 model steps at about 7 s each |

## Faster, ranked by seconds saved

1. **Mail no longer holds the finish (about 60–70 s).** This is the fix I just wrote; it also addresses the missing discount.
2. **End the specification worker the moment the revision list is read (about 40 s).** Everything else waits on this stage, so it is the best lever after mail.
3. **Cut the wait after each click on the tender portal (about 20–30 s).** A click there takes 5.6 s median, against 0.7 s on the ERP and 1.1 s on the mail.
4. **Bound the slow material reads (30–80 s in bad runs).** Open a second tab for a straggler, as mail already does, and skip the second pass when the first covered every view.
5. **One tool call from the last position to the signing step (about 25 s).** Today it is six separate model steps.

With 1 to 5 the budget is roughly 8 + 25 + 15 + 20 + 30 + 15 s, just under 2 minutes. Going well below that needs reading pages over plain HTTP, which you deferred.

## Cheaper

The workers used 526k input tokens, only 18 % of them cached:

| Part | Input tokens | Share |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ERP material reads | 251k | 48 % |
| Mail | 89k | 17 % |
| ERP search | 83k | 16 % |
| Bid form | 61k | 12 % |
| Tender read | 25k | 5 % |

- **Material reads (saves about 150k):** each of 10 materials costs 22k because the page text is sent back to the worker on 4 requests. A separate reader already extracts the facts, so the worker only needs titles and coverage.
- **Mail (saves about 70k):** the single-kind fallback searches disappear with the survey fix; one of them alone cost 72k.
- **Cache hits:** put the text shared by all material workers ahead of the material number, so the prefix cache hits more than 18 % of the time.
- **Clef for yes/no checks:** at about 1 s per call it can answer "is this the signing step" or "did the list change" instead of a Qwen step.

Now checking the local run of the mail fix.

class SurveyListTest(unittest.TestCase):
    VIEW = '[e8 textbox "Search"]\\n[e9 button "Go"]'

    def test_one_call_lists_a_folder_for_every_topic(self):
        session = SimpleNamespace(name="mail", site={"url": "https://mail.test/"}, trace=Events(), view=self.VIEW,
                                  page=SimpleNamespace(url="https://mail.test/"))
        asked: list[tuple[str, str, str | None]] = []
        found = {"T-1 Tariffs": [("Tariffs T-1 | 3 Jan", [("Tariffs T-1", "/messages/7")])],
                 "T-1 Rates": [("Rates T-1 | 2 Jan", [("Rates T-1", "/messages/5")]),
                               ("Tariffs T-1 | 3 Jan", [("Tariffs T-1", "/messages/7")])]}

        async def search_rows(sess, field_ref, query, submit_ref=None):
            asked.append((field_ref, query, submit_ref))
            sess.view = '[e3 link "Home"]\\n[e11 textbox "Search"]\\n[e12 button "Go"]'  # refs change with the view
            return listing(*found[query]), f"Search for {query!r}"

        async def run():
            index: list[rm.SurveyRow] = []
            tool = rm.list_tool(index)
            ctx = SimpleNamespace(deps=SimpleNamespace(session=session))
            first = await tool(ctx, "e8", ["T-1 Tariffs", "T-1 Rates"], "e9")
            again = await tool(ctx, "e11", ["T-1 Rates"], "e12")
            with self.assertRaises(rm.Stuck):  # twice nothing new: the survey has what there is
                await tool(ctx, "e11", ["T-1 Rates"], "e12")
            return index, first, again

        with patch.object(rm.site_tools, "search_rows", search_rows):
            index, first, again = asyncio.run(run())
        # the field and button are found again by their names after each search
        self.assertEqual(asked[:2], [("e8", "T-1 Tariffs", "e9"), ("e11", "T-1 Rates", "e12")])
        self.assertEqual([row.url for row in index], ["https://mail.test/messages/7", "https://mail.test/messages/5"])
        self.assertIn("'T-1 Rates': 2 rows, 1 new", first)
        self.assertIn("Nothing new", again)

class Trace:
    def __init__(self, directory: str | None = None):
        global CURRENT
        CURRENT = self
        self.key: list[str] = []
        self.started = self.last = time.monotonic()
        directory = directory or os.environ.get("TRACE_DIR", "traces")
        Path(directory).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.path = Path(directory) / time.strftime("run-%Y%m%d-%H%M%S.jsonl")
        self.file = self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8")

    # events that mark a phase or a failure; repeated in one block at the end of the run (summary())
    KEY_KINDS = {"start", "done", "stopped", "problem", "start_failed", "spec_done", "tender_facts", "mail_kind",
                 "answer", "summary_check", "last_chance", "crashed", "decision_disputed", "helper_error"}

    def event(self, worker: str, kind: str, quiet: bool = False, **data) -> None:
        self.last = time.monotonic()
        seconds = round(self.last - self.started, 2)
        self.file.write(json.dumps({"t": seconds, "worker": worker, "kind": kind, **data}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
        self.file.flush()
        if quiet:  # file only, e.g. the full page views
            return
        brief = " ".join(f"{k}={str(v)[:120]!r}" if isinstance(v, str) else f"{k}={v}" for k, v in data.items())
        print(f"[{seconds:7.1f}s] {worker:<15} {kind:<12} {brief}", flush=True)
        if kind in self.KEY_KINDS:
            self.key.append(f"[{seconds:7.1f}s] {worker:<15} {kind:<12} {brief[:150]}")

The mail fix is in and the sandbox test on public data is running now (`run_de4a018b0666cfbc`, about 4.5 minutes in at the last check); its score is not back yet. The full unit suite is also re-running in the background after the last edits.

**What the fix does**
- **Cause of the 84.8:** the survey searched each folder with the tender reference alone. The public mailbox cuts such a broad search short and asks for the reference plus a subject word, so the approval was never listed and the bid went out without the discount.
- **Search:** the model now runs one search per record topic in each folder, all in a single tool call.
- **Sorting:** the model that sorts rows into record kinds had been keeping only one version of a record (for the exchange-rate fixing it kept the one dated after the scenario date and dropped the valid one). It is now asked once about any row it left out.

**Local run on the public sites (stops before signing)**
- All nine record kinds were found by the survey, and the 5 % discount is back.
- Research finished at 173 s instead of 292 s; the whole run reached the signing step at 254 s instead of 336 s.

- I could not score the answer locally: `checks/score.py` is not on this machine.

**One addition you did not ask for:** the run summary now ends with the page waits per website. In the sandbox a click on the tender portal takes 4–6 s against 0.7 s locally, and the bid form plus signing takes about 100 s there; this will show which wait is responsible. def reset_loop(self, guard: bool = False, stop: bool = False) -> None:
        """A new worker run starts: forget the page states of the previous one and set its loop options."""
        self.states, self.loop_hits, self.loop_guard, self.stop_on_loop = [], 0, guard, stop

    def _loop_check(self, url: str) -> str:
        """Record the current page state; a warning for the model when it is a loop, or Stuck when told to stop."""
        if not self.loop_guard:
            return ""
        signature = hashlib.sha1(f"{url}\n{REF_TOKEN.sub('e', self.view)}".encode()).hexdigest()
        self.states.append(signature)
        repeats = self.states[-STATE_WINDOW:].count(signature)
        if repeats < STATE_REPEATS:

    task, _ = contract.load_run()

class MailboxTab(unittest.TestCase):
    """The TAN is fetched in a webmail tab the research used last, reloaded while the bid form is filled in."""

    def session(self, name: str, closed: bool = False, ok: bool = True):
        events: list[str] = []

        async def revive():
            events.append("revive")

        async def goto(url):
            events.append("goto")
        page = SimpleNamespace(url="https://mail.test/", is_closed=lambda: closed)
        return SimpleNamespace(name=name, ok=ok, page=page, lock=asyncio.Lock(), revive=revive, _goto=goto,
                               trace=Trace(tempfile.mkdtemp()), events=events)

    def adopt(self, sessions, busy: bool = False):
        import submit

        async def run():
            first = self.session("mail")
            box = submit.Mailbox(first, SimpleNamespace(tender_reference="T-1"), time.monotonic() + 600)
            if busy:
                await box.lock.acquire()
            box.adopt(sessions)
            if box.warming is not None:
                await box.warming
            return box, first
        return asyncio.run(run())

    def test_the_last_usable_research_tab_is_taken_and_reloaded(self):
        tabs = [self.session("mail:mail1"), self.session("mail:mail2"), self.session("mail:mail3", closed=True)]
        box, first = self.adopt(tabs)
        self.assertEqual(box.session.name, "mail:mail2")
        self.assertEqual((tabs[1].events, first.events), (["revive", "goto"], []))

    def test_without_research_tabs_its_own_tab_is_reloaded(self):
        box, first = self.adopt([])
        self.assertEqual((box.session.name, first.events), ("mail", ["revive", "goto"]))
        box, first = self.adopt([self.session("mail:mail1", ok=False)])
        self.assertEqual(box.session.name, "mail")

    def test_a_running_lookup_keeps_its_tab(self):
        box, first = self.adopt([self.session("mail:mail1")], busy=True)
        self.assertEqual((box.session.name, box.warming), ("mail", None))

The sandbox test came back at **quality 100** (`run_de4a018b0666cfbc`, 5:49, $0.113): the discount is read again and every position scored full points. It is not faster than before, though, and nothing is committed.

## Why it was still slow

| Cause | Cost in this run | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Three of the four sites did not open their first tab for 50–110 s (the tender portal only at 120 s). The platform API was timing out at the same time, so this looks like platform load, not our code. | about 60–100 s | no change made |
| The mail survey stopped after the first folder, so six record kinds fell back to slow single searches and research ended at 273 s. My new "nothing new twice, stop" rule is the likely cause, but the start of that log was cut off, so I can't confirm it. | about 90 s | changed, being checked now |
| The first TAN lookup ran out of its 16 steps without finding the message; a second TAN had to be requested. | about 35 s | changed, not yet run |

## What I changed after the run

- **Survey:** a repeated listing of an unchanged page is now answered without searching again. Each listing returns the current page so the next folder can be opened. The survey only stops after three empty lists in a row.
- **TAN:** the lookup now starts from the mailbox's start page instead of wherever the research left the tab (a search result or another folder).
- **Run summary:** it now ends with the page waits per website, to find out which wait makes clicks on the tender portal slow in the sandbox.
- **`dev/survey_check.py`:** a new script that runs only the mail survey in several tabs. It is running against the public mailbox right now to see whether both folders get listed.

The unit tests for the mail and mailbox changes pass. The full suite last passed (333 tests) before these three post-run changes, and none of them has been in a sandbox run yet.

## Under 2 minutes

That is not reachable with these fixes alone. With healthy site starts I estimate research at about 100 s and form plus signing at about 60 s, so roughly 2:40–2:50. Getting to 2:00 needs the specification and ERP chain shortened as well; well below that needs plain-HTTP reading, which you deferred.

Once the survey check reports, I'll run the full suite again. A second sandbox run would verify the three changes — you asked for one test, so say if you want it.
Okay first, try to reach 240-250. We'll think about remaining steps later.

import asyncio, os, time
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

async def main():
    url = os.environ["CHALLENGE_SITE_MAIL_URL"]
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        browser = await p.chromium.launch(headless=True)
        for i in range(4):
            ctx = await browser.new_context()
            page = await ctx.new_page()
            reqs = []
            page.on("request", lambda r, reqs=reqs: reqs.append((time.monotonic(), "req", r.method, r.url[:90])))
            page.on("requestfinished", lambda r, reqs=reqs: reqs.append((time.monotonic(), "done", r.method, r.url[:90])))
            page.on("requestfailed", lambda r, reqs=reqs: reqs.append((time.monotonic(), "FAILED", r.method, r.url[:90])))
            t = time.monotonic()
            try:
                await page.goto(url, timeout=20000, wait_until="domcontentloaded")
                print(i, "goto ok", round(time.monotonic() - t, 2), page.url[:80])
            except Exception as e:
                print(i, "goto FAILED", round(time.monotonic() - t, 2), str(e).splitlines()[0][:100])
            for at, what, method, u in reqs[:14]:
                print("    ", round(at - t, 2), what, method, u)
            await ctx.close()
        await browser.close()

asyncio.run(main())
EOF

SURVEY_GOAL = """\
List this mailbox's messages for tender {reference}, in every folder the mailbox has (for example inbox and
archive). In each folder call list_messages once with the mailbox's search field and one query per topic: the
reference {reference} together with each of these topic words: {topics}. A search combines its words with AND, and
a search that is too broad is cut short or refused, so the reference alone is not enough; if the mailbox says how
it wants to be searched, follow that. list_messages runs every query, pages each result list to its end and
remembers all rows. With no arguments it takes the list the folder shows as it is (for a folder without a
search). Do not open messages: the rows are sorted into records afterwards. As soon as every folder is listed,
return a one-line summary."""


def _same_control(view: str, control: tuple[str, str] | None) -> str | None:
    """The ref of the control with this kind and name in a newer view (refs change with every view)."""
    if control is None:
        return None
    return next((ref for ref, kind, name in REF_LINE.findall(view) if (kind, name) == control), None)

        if left[0] is not None and left[0] == shown(session):

            return ("Nothing was done on the page since the last listing: its rows are remembered, and listing it "

                if listing is None:

                lines.append(f"- {query!r}: {len(listing.rows)} rows, {new} new{notes}")
        else:

            lines.append(f"- the list as shown: {len(listing.rows)} rows, {added} new")
        idle[0] = 0 if added else idle[0] + 1

        if idle[0] >= 3:  # three lists in a row with nothing new: the survey has what there is

        view = await session.look()  # the page as it is now: its refs are the ones to use for the next folder
        left[0] = shown(session)
        return ("\n".join(lines) + f"\nRemembered {added} new row(s), {len(index)} in all so far."
                + (" Nothing new here." if not added else "")
                + "\nThese searches are done, also the one the page shows now. If a folder is not listed yet, "
                "open it and list it the same way; otherwise return.\n\nThe page now:\n" + view)

    return list_messages

            session.page.url = "https://mail.test/?folder=old"
            session.view = '[e5 textbox "Search"]\\n[e6 button "Go"]'

    def test_one_call_lists_a_folder_for_every_topic(self):

            tool = rm.list_tool(index)
            ctx = SimpleNamespace(deps=SimpleNamespace(session=session))

            session.view += '\\n[e20 link "Old mail"]'  # a folder menu opened, the folder is still the same

        self.assertIn("Nothing was done on the page", again)
        self.assertIn("the folder has not changed", same)
        self.assertIn("Listed at https://mail.test/?folder=old", other)

    def test_a_list_asked_for_again_and_again_ends_the_survey(self):

- **Mail survey:** whether it now lists both folders in one pass. In my local check with three surveys side by side, two listed both folders, in 55 s and 69 s. The third was still on its first folder when its 120 s limit ran out. The mail site was hanging on page loads during that check.

- **Page waits:** the summary will show where the tender portal clicks lose time.

One further fix is not in those two runs. A message page that hangs in the survey is now reopened after 15 s (up to three tries) instead of being waited on for 75 s; hung message pages cost two surveys a record kind each in the local check. Mail unit tests pass with it.
